q.en: Company A (a DRAM chip maker) and Company B (a toll-road operator) both trade at a trailing P/E of 15x this year. Company A just swung from two years of losses to its best profit ever, driven by a spike in chip prices. Company B's profit has grown steadily 4-6% a year for a decade. Which P/E deserves more scrutiny before you trust it?
q.zh: A公司（DRAM晶片製造商）和B公司（收費站經營商）今年的本益比都是15倍。A公司剛從連續兩年虧損翻轉成史上最佳獲利，主因是晶片價格飆漲。B公司的獲利十年來每年穩定成長4%到6%。在信任這兩個本益比之前，哪一個更需要進一步檢查？

opts.en: Company B's, because steady growth is suspicious.
opts.zh: B公司的，因為穩定成長反而可疑。

opts.en: Company A's, because this year's profit may be a cyclical peak, not a durable level.
opts.zh: A公司的，因為今年的獲利可能是循環高峰，不是能維持的水準。

opts.en: Neither — a 15x P/E means the same thing regardless of the business.
opts.zh: 都不用，本益比15倍不管什麼生意都代表同一件事。

exp.en: Company A just came off two loss-making years and hit a profit peak in the same year you're looking at its P/E — that is close to the classic setup for a cyclical top, where the “E” is about to fall back down, not stay flat. Company B's decade of steady growth makes its current profit a much more trustworthy base for a multiple.
exp.zh: A公司才剛結束連續兩年虧損，就在你檢視本益比的同一年衝上獲利高峰——這幾乎是循環高峰的典型情境，分母的獲利接下來很可能會回落，而不是維持不變。B公司十年穩定成長，讓它目前的獲利是一個可信得多的倍數計算基礎。

q.en: Why does this framework put “what has the market already assumed” before “how do you judge”?
q.zh: 為什麼這套框架把「市場已經假設了什麼」放在「怎麼下判斷」之前？

opts.en: Because market expectations never matter for long-term investors.
opts.zh: 因為市場預期對長期投資人來說根本不重要。

opts.en: Because your judgment has to be measured against what's already priced in, not against the raw quality of the business alone.
opts.zh: 因為你的判斷必須拿來跟已經反映在價格裡的東西比較，不能只憑生意本身的品質。

opts.en: Because the order doesn't actually matter, it's just convention.
opts.zh: 因為順序其實不重要，只是慣例而已。

exp.en: A judgment formed only from business quality, without checking what the price already assumes, can't tell you whether today is a good time to act — a great business at a price assuming perfection and a great business at a price assuming mediocrity call for opposite decisions.
exp.zh: 一個只從生意品質形成、卻沒有檢查價格已經假設了什麼的判斷，沒辦法告訴你現在是不是進場的好時機——一家好生意在假設完美的價格下，跟同一家好生意在假設平庸的價格下，會導向完全相反的決定。

q.en: A friend says: “I think this stock will do well because the company is well managed.” What is missing for this to count as a falsifiable view?
q.zh: 朋友說：「我覺得這檔股票會表現不錯，因為公司經營得很好。」這句話要成為一個可證偽的判斷，缺了什麼？

opts.en: Nothing — good management is a sufficient reason.
opts.zh: 什麼都不缺——經營得好就是充分的理由。

opts.en: A specific, checkable fact that would prove the view wrong if it occurred.
opts.zh: 一個具體、可查證的事實，一旦出現就會證明這個判斷是錯的。

opts.en: A price target, since that's the only thing that makes a view real.
opts.zh: 一個目標價，因為那才是讓判斷變得真實的關鍵。

exp.en: “Well managed” is vague enough to survive almost any outcome, good or bad, without ever being tested. A falsifiable version names a specific metric and threshold — for example, a renewal rate or a market-share figure — that would change the view if breached.
exp.zh: 「經營得好」這句話模糊到不管結果好壞都能存活下來，永遠不會被檢驗。可證偽的版本要指名一個具體的指標與門檻——例如續約率或市佔率——一旦跌破，判斷就要改變。

q.en: A company has an 80% market share and a beloved brand inside its industry, but the entire industry is being replaced by a new technology from outside it. What kind of analysis is most likely to miss this danger?
q.zh: 一家公司在自己的產業裡市佔率高達八成、品牌形象也很好，但整個產業正在被產業之外的新技術取代。哪一種分析最容易漏掉這個危險？

opts.en: Analysis that only looks at the company's own competitive position within its industry, without checking threats from outside it.
opts.zh: 只看公司在自己產業內部競爭地位的分析，沒有檢查來自產業之外的威脅。

opts.en: Analysis that checks the industry's supply and demand balance every quarter.
opts.zh: 每季都檢查產業供需平衡的分析。

opts.en: Analysis that compares the company's ROIC to its cost of capital.
opts.zh: 比較公司ROIC與資金成本的分析。

exp.en: A moat measures your position relative to competitors inside the same industry. It says nothing about whether the entire industry is itself being displaced by something outside it (the Kodak story above is exactly this pattern) — that requires a separate, deliberate check for substitution from outside the circle.
exp.zh: 護城河衡量的是你在同一個產業裡相對於競爭者的位置，完全沒有回答整個產業是不是正在被產業之外的東西取代（上面柯達的故事正是這個模式）——這需要另外、刻意地檢查來自圈外的替代威脅。

q.en: Which of the following is the best example of a falsifiable view, in the sense this lesson uses the term?
q.zh: 以下哪一個最符合這一課所講的「可證偽判斷」？

opts.en: “This is a great company with a bright future.”
opts.zh: 「這是一家很棒的公司，前景光明。」

opts.en: “I will act now, and if gross margin falls below 40% for two consecutive quarters, I will treat the thesis as broken.”
opts.zh: 「我現在進場，如果毛利率連續兩季跌破40%，我就會認定這個論點已經破局。」

opts.en: “The stock could go up or down depending on the market.”
opts.zh: 「這檔股票可能漲也可能跌，要看市場而定。」

exp.en: The second option names a specific number and a specific condition under which the writer commits to changing their mind — that is what makes it falsifiable. The other two are true of almost any stock at almost any time and can never be shown to have failed.
exp.zh: 第二個選項指名了一個具體數字，以及在什麼條件下作者會承諾改變想法——這正是讓它可證偽的關鍵。另外兩句話對幾乎任何一檔股票、在幾乎任何時候都成立，永遠無法被證明失敗。

q.en: A pre-revenue biotech company's entire value depends on a single clinical trial's binary outcome, expected in six months. How well does the five-question framework in this lesson apply here?
q.zh: 一家還沒有營收的生技公司，整個公司價值取決於六個月後即將揭曉的一次臨床試驗的二元結果。這一課的五個問題框架，在這個情境下適用性如何？

opts.en: Perfectly — every industry and company can be analyzed the same way.
opts.zh: 完全適用——每一個產業和公司都能用同一套方法分析。

opts.en: Poorly — questions like “does the company earn above its cost of capital” can't be answered without an operating history, so a probability-weighted scenario approach fits better.
opts.zh: 不太適用——「公司賺得比資金成本多嗎」這類問題，在沒有營運歷史的情況下根本答不出來，改用機率加權的情境分析會更合適。

opts.en: It doesn't matter, since valuation is asked last regardless.
opts.zh: 沒差，反正估值本來就排在最後一個問題。

exp.en: This lesson explicitly names this as a boundary condition: the five questions assume there's an established industry and operating history to study. A binary, pre-revenue outcome doesn't give you the data those questions need, so forcing this framework onto it produces false precision rather than insight.
exp.zh: 這一課明白指出這是這套工具的邊界：五個問題的前提是有一個成形的產業與可研究的營運歷史。一個尚未產生營收、結果二元的情境，給不出這些問題需要的數據，硬套這套框架只會產生虛假的精確感，而不是真正的洞察。

q.en: After Cisco's stock peaked around 2000, the company kept selling networking equipment and remained profitable for the next two decades, yet twenty years later the share price was still only about half its 2000 level. What does this best illustrate?
q.zh: 思科股價在2000年見頂之後，公司接下來二十年仍持續銷售網路設備並維持獲利，二十年後股價卻仍然只有2000年的一半左右。這最能說明什麼？

opts.en: Cisco was secretly a bad business the whole time.
opts.zh: 思科其實一直是一家爛公司，只是沒被發現。

opts.en: A genuinely good business can still be a bad investment if the price already assumed an extreme, hard-to-beat future.
opts.zh: 就算是一門真正的好生意，如果價格早就假設了一個極端、難以超越的未來，也可能是一筆糟糕的投資。

opts.en: Networking equipment as an industry disappeared after 2000.
opts.zh: 網路設備這個產業在2000年後就消失了。

exp.en: Cisco remained a real, profitable company — the business (layer 1) held up reasonably well. What failed was the price (layer 3), which by 2000 had already priced in a scale of dominance no realistic execution could match, leaving little room for the stock to be rewarded even for continued good performance.
exp.zh: 思科始終是一家真實、獲利的公司——生意本身（第一層）表現得還算過得去。真正出問題的是價格（第三層），2000年時的價格早就已經反映了一種再怎麼完美執行都難以企及的霸主規模，即使公司後來持續有不錯的表現，股價也沒什麼被獎勵的空間。

q.en: “HarborSteel,” a commodity steel producer with a decade of ROIC averaging below its cost of capital, just posted its best year in a decade (ROIC 24%) as steel prices spiked, and the stock is up about 80% in six months. A friend says “the moat clearly got stronger.” What's the strongest response?
q.zh: 「港灣鋼鐵」是一家原物料鋼鐵生產商，過去十年ROIC平均低於資金成本，今年因為鋼價飆升交出十年來最好的成績（ROIC 24%），股價半年漲了約八成。朋友說：「護城河明顯變強了。」你最好的回應是什麼？

opts.en: Agree — ROIC quadrupling is hard evidence of a stronger moat.
opts.zh: 同意——ROIC變成四倍就是護城河變強的鐵證。

opts.en: A commodity producer's competitive position (undifferentiated product, no switching costs) doesn't change in twelve months — this pattern looks like a cyclical price spike, not a durable moat change.
opts.zh: 原物料生產商的競爭地位（產品無差異化、沒有轉換成本）不會在十二個月內改變——這個模式看起來像循環性的價格飆升，不是耐久的護城河改變。

opts.en: It doesn't matter either way, since the stock is already up 80%.
opts.zh: 反正股價都已經漲八成了，怎麼解讀不重要。

exp.en: A moat is a structural, industry-level property — it doesn't materialize in one year just because a commodity price spiked. Ten years of sub-cost-of-capital returns is a much longer, more reliable signal about the underlying business than one year driven by an external price swing. The right follow-up question is not “how good is this company” but “where in the steel cycle are we, and what happens to that 24% when prices normalise?”
exp.zh: 護城河是一種結構性、產業層級的特質——不會因為商品價格飆漲一年就突然出現。十年低於資金成本的報酬率，是一個比單一年度、由外部價格波動驅動的數字，更長期、更可靠得多的訊號。真正該追問的不是「這家公司有多好」，而是「現在站在鋼鐵循環的哪個位置，鋼價回到常態時那個24%會變成什麼」。

q.en: You just finished analyzing a company and wrote: “This is a solid business with both opportunities and risks.” Per this lesson, what is the biggest problem with stopping here?
q.zh: 你剛分析完一家公司，寫下：「這是一門穩健的生意，有機會也有風險。」照這一課的標準，停在這裡最大的問題是什麼？

opts.en: Nothing — this is an honest, balanced conclusion.
opts.zh: 沒問題——這是一個誠實、平衡的結論。

opts.en: It contains no actionable, falsifiable view — it can never be shown to have been wrong, so it can never be updated either.
opts.zh: 它沒有交出任何可行動、可證偽的判斷——永遠無法被證明是錯的，因此也永遠無法被更新。

opts.en: It should have started with the valuation instead.
opts.zh: 應該從估值開始寫才對。

exp.en: “Opportunities and risks on both sides” fits nearly any outcome after the fact, which means it can survive contrary evidence forever without forcing a re-think. The actual output this framework asks for is a one-sentence view plus a specific condition that would prove it wrong.
exp.zh: 「有機會也有風險」這種說法，事後不管發生什麼結果都套得上，代表它可以永遠承受反面證據，卻不會逼你重新思考。這套框架真正要求交出的產出，是一句判斷，加上一個具體、會證明它錯了的條件。

q.en: A company's gross margin holds steady, but its operating margin falls year over year. What is the most likely explanation?
q.zh: 一家公司毛利率維持穩定，但營業利益率逐年下滑。最可能的原因是？

opts.en: SG&A or R&D spending grew faster than revenue
opts.zh: SG&A 或研發費用的成長速度快過營收

opts.en: Inventory increased
opts.zh: 存貨增加了

opts.en: The stock price fell
opts.zh: 股價下跌

opts.en: Cash on the balance sheet increased
opts.zh: 資產負債表上的現金增加了

exp.en: Stable gross margin means cost of goods sold stayed proportional to revenue. A falling operating margin below that means the layer of costs below gross profit — sales, marketing, R&D, admin — is growing faster than revenue, which is a spending-decision story, not a pricing-power story.
exp.zh: 毛利率穩定，代表銷貨成本占營收的比例沒有變。毛利之下的營業利益率卻在下滑，代表毛利之後那一層費用——業務、行銷、研發、行政——成長速度快過營收，這是支出決策的故事，不是定價能力的故事。

q.en: A company's NOPAT was $40M on $250M of invested capital in Year 1, and $46M on $270M of invested capital in Year 2. What is incremental ROIC?
q.zh: 一家公司第一年 NOPAT 為 4,000 萬美元、投入資本 2.5 億美元；第二年 NOPAT 為 4,600 萬美元、投入資本 2.7 億美元。增量 ROIC 最接近多少？

opts.en: About 17%
About 16%
About 30%
About 6%

exp.en: Incremental ROIC = ΔNOPAT ÷ Δinvested capital = ($46M − $40M) ÷ ($270M − $250M) = $6M ÷ $20M = 30%. Both 16% and 17% are the average ROIC of Year 1 and Year 2 respectively — useful, but not the number that tells you how good the newest capital is.
exp.zh: 增量 ROIC ＝ ΔNOPAT ÷ Δ投入資本 ＝（4,600 萬 − 4,000 萬）÷（2.7 億 − 2.5 億）＝ 600 萬 ÷ 2,000 萬 ＝ 30%。16% 與 17% 分別是第一年、第二年的平均 ROIC——有用，但不是告訴你最新資本有多好的那個數字。

q.en: FCF ÷ net income fell from 0.9 to 0.55 at the same time capital expenditure rose sharply and incremental ROIC rose from 12% to 22%. What does this most likely indicate?
q.zh: FCF ÷ 淨利從 0.9 降到 0.55，同時資本支出大幅上升、增量 ROIC 從 12% 升到 22%。這最可能代表什麼？

opts.en: Earnings quality is deteriorating and the stock should be avoided
opts.zh: 獲利品質正在惡化，應該避開

opts.en: This may be productive, expansionary spending — a falling ratio is not automatically bad when the incremental return is high
opts.zh: 這可能是高產出的擴張性支出——增量報酬夠高時，比率下滑不必然是壞事

opts.en: The company is almost certainly manipulating its accounts
opts.zh: 公司幾乎一定在做假帳

opts.en: Falling cash means bankruptcy risk is rising sharply
opts.zh: 現金下滑代表破產風險大幅升高

exp.en: This is exactly the Atlas Components pattern from the worked example: a rising incremental ROIC well above the base rate means the capital funding that lower ratio is earning strong returns, which is the visible cost of investing in growth, not a quality warning by itself.
exp.zh: 這正是逐步範例裡亞特拉斯零組件的型態：增量 ROIC 明顯高於基礎報酬率，代表撐起這個較低比率的資本，正賺到很好的報酬，這是投資成長看得見的代價，本身不是品質警訊。

q.en: Two companies have identical revenue, identical operating profit, and identical net PP&E, inventory and receivables. The only difference: Company A pays its suppliers in 30 days, Company B in 90 days. Which has the higher ROIC?
q.zh: 兩家公司的營收、營業利益、淨廠房設備、存貨、應收帳款全部一模一樣。唯一的差別是：A 公司 30 天付款給供應商，B 公司 90 天。哪一家的 ROIC 比較高？

opts.en: Company A — paying suppliers faster shows financial discipline
opts.zh: A 公司——付款快代表財務紀律好

opts.en: Company B — larger payables reduce invested capital, so the same profit sits on a smaller base
opts.zh: B 公司——應付帳款較大會縮小投入資本，同樣的利潤落在較小的基數上

opts.en: Identical — payment terms do not touch the income statement, so ROIC cannot differ
opts.zh: 完全一樣——付款條件不影響損益表，所以 ROIC 不可能有差

opts.en: Company A — because B is effectively borrowing, which raises its cost of capital
opts.zh: A 公司——因為 B 等於在借錢，資金成本會比較高

exp.en: Invested capital is net PP&E plus inventory plus receivables plus other operating assets, MINUS non-interest-bearing operating liabilities — payables included. B's suppliers are financing 90 days of its operating cycle interest-free, so B runs the identical business on less of its own capital and posts a higher ROIC. The third option is the common trap: ROIC has a balance-sheet denominator, so a change that never touches the income statement can still move it. The fourth confuses trade credit with borrowing — payables carry no interest, which is exactly why they are subtracted.
exp.zh: 投入資本＝淨廠房設備＋存貨＋應收帳款＋其他營運資產，「減去」不計息營運負債，應付帳款就在其中。B 公司的供應商等於無息幫它墊了 90 天的營運循環，所以 B 用比較少的自有資本經營一模一樣的生意，ROIC 因此較高。第三個選項是最常見的陷阱：ROIC 的分母在資產負債表上，所以一個完全不碰損益表的改變，照樣會讓它移動。第四個選項把商業信用當成借款——應付帳款不用付利息，這正是它要被扣掉的原因。

q.en: A company's EPS grew 15% while total net income grew only 5%. What is the most likely explanation?
q.zh: 一家公司 EPS 成長 15%，但總淨利只成長 5%。最可能的解釋是？

opts.en: The tax rate fell
opts.zh: 稅率下降

opts.en: A large buyback reduced the share count
opts.zh: 大量回購減少了股數

opts.en: A favorable currency move
opts.zh: 匯率帶來利多

opts.en: Gross margin improved
opts.zh: 毛利率提升

exp.en: A lower tax rate or better gross margin would raise total net income and EPS by roughly the same percentage if the share count did not change — neither explains a gap between the two growth rates on its own. Only a shrinking denominator, the share count, can make EPS outrun total profit growth.
exp.zh: 如果股數沒變，稅率下降或毛利率提升會讓總淨利與 EPS 用差不多的百分比一起成長——這兩者本身都不能解釋兩個成長率之間的落差。只有分母（股數）縮小，才能讓 EPS 跑贏總利潤的成長。

q.en: What is the biggest problem with treating EBITDA as if it were cash flow?
q.zh: 把 EBITDA 當成現金流量看待，最大的問題是什麼？

opts.en: It ignores capital expenditure and working-capital changes, so it can be mistaken for cash when it is not
opts.zh: 它沒有考慮資本支出與營運資金變化，可能被誤當成現金，但它不是

opts.en: It ignores revenue growth
opts.zh: 它沒有考慮營收成長

opts.en: It is always deliberately manipulated by the company
opts.zh: 它一定是被公司刻意操縱過的

opts.en: It is a pre-tax measure, so it is too conservative
opts.zh: 它是稅前指標，所以太保守

exp.en: A capital-heavy business can show robust EBITDA while free cash flow is thin or negative once the capital spending needed to keep the equipment running is subtracted — EBITDA simply never subtracts it.
exp.zh: 一門重資產生意可以在 EBITDA 看起來很健壯的同時，一旦扣掉維持設備運轉所需要的資本支出，自由現金流卻很薄甚至是負的——因為 EBITDA 本來就從來沒有扣掉這一項。

q.en: A stock underwent a large stock split at some point in its history. If you calculate a long-run return using an unadjusted price series that spans that split date, what is most likely to happen?
q.zh: 一檔股票曾經在歷史上執行過大比例分割。如果用一段橫跨分割日期、未還原的股價序列去算長期報酬率，最可能發生什麼？

opts.en: The return will be badly miscalculated, because the price drop caused by the split looks like a real loss in the raw series
opts.zh: 報酬率會被嚴重算錯，因為分割造成的股價下降，在原始序列裡看起來像真實的損失

opts.en: There will be no effect at all
opts.zh: 完全不會有任何影響

opts.en: There will be only a tiny, ignorable error
opts.zh: 只會有極小、可以忽略的誤差

opts.en: Using an adjusted price series would actually be more likely to introduce errors
opts.zh: 用還原後的股價序列反而更容易出錯

exp.en: A split changes the price per share without changing anything about the underlying business or the holder's wealth. An unadjusted series treats that price drop as if it were a real decline, which can distort a calculated return by a factor of several times depending on the split ratio.
exp.zh: 分割改變的是每股價格，跟底層生意、股東的財富完全無關。未還原的序列會把這次價格下降當成真實的下跌，依分割比例的不同，算出來的報酬率可能整整扭曲好幾倍。

q.en: A company has grown net income more than 10% for two straight years, but the gap between its “adjusted” earnings and GAAP net income keeps widening, mostly from adding back stock-based compensation. What should you check first?
q.zh: 一家公司連續兩年淨利成長都超過 10%，但「調整後」盈餘與 GAAP 淨利之間的落差逐年擴大，主要來自加回股份薪酬。你應該先檢查什麼？

opts.en: The trend in FCF ÷ net income, and stock-based compensation as a share of revenue
opts.zh: FCF ÷ 淨利的趨勢，以及股份薪酬占營收比重的趨勢

opts.en: Just the P/E ratio
opts.zh: 直接看本益比高不高

opts.en: The stock's recent chart pattern
opts.zh: 股價最近的技術線型

opts.en: Nothing — stock-based compensation does not touch cash, so it does not matter
opts.zh: 不用管，股份薪酬不影響現金，所以不重要

exp.en: A widening gap driven by SBC add-backs is precisely the pattern this lesson flags: SBC is non-cash but dilutive, so the FCF-to-net-income trend and the SBC-to-revenue ratio are the two numbers that tell you how much real economic cost is being waved away by the adjusted figure.
exp.zh: 由 SBC 加回撐大的落差，正是這一課要示範抓的型態：SBC 不是現金，但會稀釋股東，所以 FCF 對淨利的趨勢，加上 SBC 占營收的比重，這兩個數字才能告訴你「調整後」數字揮手帶過了多少真實的經濟成本。

q.en: A company reports revenue up 20% year over year, but its disclosed unit-shipment count is flat versus last year. What does this combination most likely tell you?
q.zh: 一家公司揭露營收年增20%，但公佈的出貨量年增卻是持平。這個組合最可能告訴你什麼？

opts.en: Demand is accelerating and the company is gaining market share
opts.zh: 需求正在加速，公司正在搶市占

opts.en: The growth is being driven mainly by price (ASP), not by more units being sold
opts.zh: 這波成長主要是靠漲價（平均售價）帶動，不是靠賣出更多數量

opts.en: The revenue figure must be a reporting error
opts.zh: 這個營收數字一定是揭露錯誤

opts.en: The company has entered a new, faster-growing market segment
opts.zh: 公司進入了一個成長更快的新市場區塊

exp.en: Flat units with rising revenue is the textbook signature of price-driven growth. That is not automatically bad, but it is a different, generally less durable growth engine than volume growth, and it needs to be evaluated on its own terms rather than assumed to be the same story as unit growth.
exp.zh: 出貨量持平但營收上升，是價格驅動型成長的教科書特徵。這不代表一定不好，但它是另一種、通常較不持久的成長引擎，跟數量驅動型成長不是同一件事，需要分開評估，不能假設兩者相同。

q.en: You build a market size top-down (from a macro spend figure) and get $50B. You build it bottom-up (summing named customers) and get $38B, a gap of roughly 24%. What should you do next?
q.zh: 你用自上而下（從總體支出數字推算）算出市場規模是500億美元，用自下而上（加總有名有姓的客戶）算出380億美元，落差大約24%。接下來你該怎麼做？

opts.en: Average the two numbers and use $44B
opts.zh: 把兩個數字平均，用440億美元

opts.en: Trust the top-down number because it is bigger and more conservative
opts.zh: 相信自上而下的數字，因為它比較大也比較保守

opts.en: Identify which specific cause explains the gap (double counting, scope mismatch, or omission) before using either number
opts.zh: 先指出是哪一個具體原因造成落差（重複計算、範圍不一致，或遺漏），再決定要用哪一個數字

opts.en: Discard both estimates and wait for a third-party research report
opts.zh: 捨棄這兩個估算，等第三方研究報告出來

exp.en: A gap this size is a signal to diagnose, not to paper over. Averaging or picking the more comfortable number both throw away the information the gap is giving you, because the reason for the mismatch usually tells you something specific about how the market should actually be defined.
exp.zh: 這種幅度的落差是要拿來診斷的訊號，不是拿來含糊帶過的雜訊。無論是取平均還是挑一個比較順眼的數字，都會把落差本來要告訴你的資訊丟掉，因為落差背後的原因，通常會告訴你這個市場到底該怎麼被正確定義。

q.en: A market's current annual size is about $140B. A base-case forecast puts its size five years out at about $280B. Using the five-year demand multiple, roughly how many times is this market expected to grow — and what annual growth rate does that imply?
q.zh: 一個市場目前的年規模大約1,400億美元。基準情境預測五年後的規模大約2,800億美元。用五年需求倍數計算，這個市場預期大約成長幾倍，又隱含每年多少的成長率？

opts.en: About 2.0x, which implies roughly 40% growth a year
opts.zh: 大約2.0倍，隱含每年大約40%的成長

opts.en: About 2.0x, which implies roughly 15% compound growth a year
opts.zh: 大約2.0倍，隱含每年大約15%的複合成長

opts.en: About 4.0x, since the market adds $140B in each of the two halves of the period
opts.zh: 大約4.0倍，因為這段期間的前後兩半各增加1,400億美元

opts.en: About 1.0x — the market is flat once the base year is taken into account
opts.zh: 大約1.0倍——把基期考慮進去之後，這個市場其實是持平的

exp.en: The five-year demand multiple is the future TAM divided by the current TAM: 280 divided by 140 is 2.0x. The second step is the one most people skip — a doubling spread over five years is about 15% compound growth a year (1.15 to the fifth power is roughly 2.0), not the 40% the raw multiple can feel like. Converting the multiple back into an annual rate is what makes the forecast checkable against next year's actual data.
exp.zh: 五年需求倍數就是未來TAM除以目前TAM：2,800除以1,400等於2.0倍。第二步才是多數人會跳過的：五年翻一倍，等於每年大約複合成長15%（1.15的五次方大約是2.0），而不是這個倍數乍看給人的40%那種感覺。把倍數換算回年化成長率，正是讓這個預測能拿明年的實際資料去查核的關鍵動作。

q.en: A supplier's orders jump from 5% growth to 35% growth in a single quarter, right after its customers announce a price increase for the coming year, and the supplier discloses that channel inventory weeks are also climbing. Which type of demand does this best describe?
q.zh: 一家供應商的訂單成長率，在客戶宣布明年要漲價之後的那一季，突然從5%跳到35%，同時供應商揭露的通路庫存周數也在上升。這最符合哪一種需求？

opts.en: Structural demand
opts.zh: 結構性需求

opts.en: Cyclical demand
opts.zh: 週期性需求

opts.en: One-off, pull-forward demand ahead of an expected price or supply change
opts.zh: 因應預期漲價或供給變化而提前拉貨的一次性需求

opts.en: A permanent step-up in the addressable market
opts.zh: 可觸及市場規模的永久性跳升

exp.en: A sudden order spike tied directly to an announced price increase, combined with rising channel inventory, is the classic stockpiling pattern. It borrows demand from future quarters rather than adding to it, and it is usually followed by an air pocket once the pulled-forward inventory works through the channel.
exp.zh: 訂單突然暴增又直接連著一則漲價公告，同時通路庫存又在上升，這是典型的囤貨模式。它是把未來幾季的需求提前挪用，而不是真的增加需求，通常在被提前拉走的庫存被通路消化完之後，會接著出現需求真空期。

q.en: An industry product has reached about 78% penetration among its original target customer segment, and unit growth has slowed sharply. A new, lower-cost version has just been introduced that opens the product to a much larger group of potential buyers who could not afford it before. What is the most defensible read?
q.zh: 一個產業的產品在原本的目標客群裡，滲透率已經到大約78%，出貨量成長明顯放緩。這時剛推出一款成本更低的新版本，讓一大群原本買不起的潛在買家也能購買。什麼樣的判讀最站得住腳？

opts.en: Growth is over because penetration already crossed 70 percent
opts.zh: 成長已經結束，因為滲透率已經超過七成

opts.en: A second S-curve may be starting against a larger denominator, so total growth could continue even though growth in the original segment is topping out
opts.zh: 第二條S曲線可能正對著一個更大的分母展開，所以就算原本客群的成長已經到頂，整體成長仍可能延續

opts.en: The low-cost version proves the company is losing pricing power
opts.zh: 推出低價版證明公司正在失去訂價權

opts.en: Penetration figures become meaningless once a new product version exists
opts.zh: 一旦出現新版本，滲透率數字就沒有意義了

exp.en: The roughly 35/70 ceiling heuristic applies to one defined customer segment at one price point, not to every future variant of the product. A new lower price point that unlocks a larger buyer pool is exactly the second-S-curve pattern this lesson describes, and it deserves active investigation before concluding growth is finished.
exp.zh: 大約35／70的天花板門檻，是針對一個定義好的客群、在一個價位帶下適用，不是針對這項產品未來所有可能的版本。一個能解鎖更大買家群的新低價位版本，正好符合這一課描述的第二條S曲線模式，值得主動查證，而不是先斷定成長已經結束。

q.en: Two companies serve the same end-market with genuinely strong, well-documented demand growth. One trades at a much higher valuation multiple than the other. Which statement is most defensible?
q.zh: 兩家公司服務同一個終端市場，需求成長都很強勁、證據也很扎實。其中一家的估值倍數比另一家高出很多。哪一句話最站得住腳？

opts.en: Strong, well-documented demand growth alone tells you the cheaper one must be the better buy
opts.zh: 光憑扎實的強勁需求成長，就能斷定比較便宜的那家一定是比較好的投資

opts.en: Demand strength explains why an industry might grow, but not which company captures the resulting profit or how much of that is already priced in, and those are separate questions
opts.zh: 需求強勁能解釋一個產業為什麼會成長，但不能回答哪家公司能留住由此而來的利潤、或市場已經把多少反映進股價，這是另外的問題

opts.en: The higher-multiple company must be overvalued
opts.zh: 估值倍數比較高的那家一定被高估了

opts.en: Valuation differences within the same end-market are always mispricing
opts.zh: 同一個終端市場裡的估值差異一定是定價錯誤

exp.en: This lesson deliberately stops short of answering who captures the profit or what the market has priced in, because those depend on the value chain and on expectations, not on demand alone. Treating strong demand as a complete investment case skips two questions this course answers separately.
exp.zh: 這一課刻意不去回答誰能留住利潤、或市場已經反映了多少，因為那要看價值鏈跟市場預期，不是光靠需求就能回答。把強勁需求當成一個完整的投資理由，等於跳過了這套框架後面另外處理的兩個問題。

q.en: A component maker draws 70% of revenue from three large operators who buy out of their annual capital budgets, and 30% from thousands of small businesses who buy out of their own operating cash flow. End usage of the product is growing in both channels. What does the 70% carry that the 30% does not?
q.zh: 一家零組件廠有70%的營收來自三家大型業者，它們是從年度資本預算裡撥錢採購；另外30%來自數千家小型企業，它們是用自己的營運現金流採購。這項產品在兩邊的終端使用量都在成長。相對於那30%，這70%多帶了什麼？

opts.en: Nothing structural — once end usage is genuinely growing, who the buyer happens to be is a detail
opts.zh: 沒有什麼結構性的差別——只要終端使用真的在成長，買家是誰只是細節

opts.en: Demand that three boards can revise in three meetings, so it can stop long before the underlying use of the product does
opts.zh: 這是三個董事會開三次會就能改掉的需求，所以它可能在產品的實際使用量下滑之前很久就先停掉

opts.en: A pure pricing risk — large customers always negotiate lower prices, which is the main thing concentration costs you
opts.zh: 純粹是價格風險——大客戶一定殺價，這就是集中度帶來的主要代價

opts.en: Higher risk of bad debt, since large buyers take longer to pay than small ones
opts.zh: 呆帳風險比較高，因為大買家的付款天期比小買家長

exp.en: Concentration plus a capital-budget funding source changes the speed at which demand can turn, not automatically the odds that it turns: a capital budget is discretionary and revisable at a single meeting, while the small businesses buying out of operating cash flow only stop when their own trade slows. Note what the question does not say — that concentration is worse. A well-funded buyer purchasing something non-discretionary can be steadier than thousands of small ones. The two things to establish are how discretionary the purchase is for whoever signs, and how secure that signer's own funding is.
exp.zh: 客戶集中，加上資金來源是資本預算，改變的是需求「可以轉向的速度」，而不是自動提高「它會轉向」的機率：資本預算是可自由裁量的，一次會議就能改；而用營運現金流採購的小型企業，要等自己的生意變差才會停。也要注意這題沒有說的事——它沒有說集中一定比較差。一個資金充裕、買的又是非買不可之物的買家，可以比幾千個小買家更穩。真正要確認的是兩件事：這筆採購對簽字的人來說有多可有可無，以及簽字的那個人自己的資金有多穩。

q.en: Industry X: demand growing 20%/yr, capacity lead time 4 years, CR3 85%. Industry Y: demand growing 20%/yr, capacity lead time 3 months, CR3 15%. Which is more likely to see prices spike and stay elevated for several years?
q.zh: 產業 X：需求每年成長 20%，產能前置時間 4 年，CR3 為 85%。產業 Y：需求每年成長 20%，產能前置時間 3 個月，CR3 為 15%。哪一個比較可能出現價格飆漲、而且撐好幾年？

opts.en: Industry X
opts.zh: 產業 X

opts.en: Industry Y
opts.zh: 產業 Y

opts.en: Both equally, since demand growth is identical
opts.zh: 兩者一樣，因為需求成長率相同

opts.en: Neither - price depends only on demand growth, not supply structure
opts.zh: 都不會，因為價格只取決於需求成長率，跟供給結構無關

exp.en: Identical demand growth, completely different outcomes: the long lead time and high concentration in X mean supply cannot catch up for years, so the gap gets settled in price. The fast, fragmented supply in Y erodes any shortage almost immediately, so the same demand growth mostly shows up as more units sold at roughly unchanged prices.
exp.zh: 需求成長率一模一樣，結果卻完全不同：X 的前置時間長、集中度又高，代表供給好幾年都追不上，缺口只能用價格結清。Y 的供給快又碎片化，任何短缺幾乎會立刻被填平，同樣的需求成長大部分會變成多賣一點，價格幾乎不動。

q.en: Two industries both require over $100M of capital per new unit of capacity. In industry A there is a deep second-hand market for the asset, and used units currently change hands at prices above the cost of building new. In industry B no meaningful second-hand market exists. What do those two facts tell you?
q.zh: 兩個產業每新增一單位產能都要投入超過一億美元。產業 A 的資產有一個成交熱絡的二手市場，而且二手成交價目前高於全新打造的成本；產業 B 則幾乎不存在有意義的二手市場。這兩件事告訴你什麼？

opts.en: Both are equally well protected, because the capital requirement per unit is the same
opts.zh: 兩者保護程度一樣，因為每單位所需資本相同

opts.en: The barrier in A is weaker than the capital number suggests - a newcomer can buy used and skip the lead time, and a loser who sells does not remove capacity from the industry - while a used price above new-build cost is a late-cycle reading, not evidence of durability
opts.zh: A 的門檻比資本數字看起來弱——新進者可以買二手、直接跳過前置時間，而且輸家把資產賣掉並沒有把產能移出產業；至於二手價高過新造成本，那是循環偏晚期的讀數，不是耐久性的證據

opts.en: A is better protected, because a liquid second-hand market proves the assets hold their value
opts.zh: A 保護得比較好，因為熱絡的二手市場證明這些資產保值

opts.en: B is the riskier industry, because its owners have no way to sell if they want out
opts.zh: B 是風險比較高的那個，因為它的持有人想退出時賣不掉

exp.en: Second-hand prices do two jobs at once. As a level, a used asset trading above new-build cost means buyers are paying a premium purely to skip the queue, which is a top-of-cycle signal rather than a sign of strength - that is the misread in option 3. As a structure, a liquid used market lowers the entry barrier the capital was supposed to create and keeps failed capacity inside the industry under a new owner. Option 4 is half right about the individual owner and backwards about the industry: capacity that can genuinely die is what makes a downturn self-correcting.
exp.zh: 二手價格同時做兩件事。就水位而言，二手資產成交價高過新造成本，代表買家純粹是為了插隊而付溢價，那是循環高點的訊號而不是強勢的證據——這正是選項三的誤讀。就結構而言，一個流動性好的二手市場，會拆掉資本本來應該築起的進入門檻，並且讓失敗者的產能換個持有人繼續留在產業裡。選項四對個別持有人講對了一半，對整個產業卻講反了：產能真的會死，才會讓一場衰退具備自我修正的能力。

q.en: Five firms hold market shares of 45%, 30%, 15%, 6%, and 4%, so CR3 is 90%. The HHI for the same five shares is closest to which value?
q.zh: 五家廠商的市占率分別是 45%、30%、15%、6%、4%，所以 CR3 是 90%。同一組五個市占率的 HHI 最接近哪個數字？

exp.en: HHI sums every share squared: 45 squared plus 30 squared plus 15 squared plus 6 squared plus 4 squared = 2,025 + 900 + 225 + 36 + 16 = 3,202, closest to 3,200. That sits comfortably above the roughly 2,500 highly-concentrated line, consistent with what the 90% CR3 already implied. Note that HHI is defined firm by firm, so lumping a tail together would overstate it.
exp.zh: HHI 是把每家市占率平方後加總：45²＋30²＋15²＋6²＋4² ＝ 2,025＋900＋225＋36＋16 ＝ 3,202，最接近 3,200，明顯高於「高度集中」約 2,500 的門檻，跟 90% 的 CR3 講的是同一件事。要注意 HHI 的定義是逐家平方，把尾巴合併計算會高估結果。

q.en: Why do long-lead-time industries tend to overshoot on both the way up and the way down?
q.zh: 為什麼前置時間長的產業，漲跌兩邊都容易矯枉過正？

opts.en: Because demand is always more volatile in these industries
opts.zh: 因為這種產業的需求本來就波動比較大

opts.en: Because every player tends to order new capacity off the same signal, and it all arrives together years later
opts.zh: 因為每個玩家往往是看到同一個訊號才下單擴產，好幾年後又一起到位

opts.en: Because regulators intervene to cap prices in these industries
opts.zh: 因為這種產業的監理機關會出手限制價格

opts.en: Because these industries never have substitutes
opts.zh: 因為這種產業從來沒有替代品

exp.en: Everyone reacts to the same visible price signal at roughly the same time, but because lead time is long, none of that new capacity shows up until years later - and then it all shows up at once, turning a shortage into an eventual glut. The demand side is not what is unstable here; the delay between decision and delivery is.
exp.zh: 大家幾乎在同一時間對同一個看得見的價格訊號做出反應，但因為前置時間長，這些新產能要好幾年後才會出現——而且是一起出現，把一場短缺變成後來的一場過剩。這裡不穩定的不是需求端，而是「決策到交貨」之間的那段時間差。

q.en: You read that a chip fab is running at 97% utilization, and that industry-wide capex guidance has tripled in the last 12 months. What is the most likely 2-3 year trajectory for prices?
q.zh: 你看到一家晶圓廠利用率高達 97%，而且整個產業的資本支出財測在過去 12 個月內變成三倍。未來兩到三年，價格最可能的走勢是什麼？

opts.en: Prices and margins keep climbing indefinitely
opts.zh: 價格與利潤率會無限期持續上漲

opts.en: Prices and margins likely peak soon, then fall as the new capacity arrives
opts.zh: 價格與利潤率可能很快見頂，然後隨新產能到位而下滑

opts.en: Nothing changes, because utilization is already maxed out
opts.zh: 不會有任何變化，因為利用率已經滿載

opts.en: Impossible to know from utilization and capex alone
opts.zh: 光看利用率與資本支出無法判斷

exp.en: High utilization plus a spike in capex guidance is a leading indicator of the coming capacity wave, not proof of a stable plateau. Option 4 is the tempting hedge, but the two numbers together are exactly the pair this chapter says is readable: utilization tells you the constraint binds today, and capex guidance tells you how many people are already acting to remove it.
exp.zh: 利用率高再加上資本支出財測暴增，是即將到來的產能潮的領先訊號，不是穩定高原期的證明。選項四是很誘人的騎牆答案，但這兩個數字放在一起，正是這一課說讀得出結論的那一組：利用率告訴你限制現在有沒有被撞上，資本支出財測告訴你已經有多少人在動手把它拆掉。

q.en: A company states that it is the only supplier in the world capable of making a critical piece of equipment. Which piece of public evidence would do the most to confirm that claim?
q.zh: 一家公司宣稱自己是全世界唯一做得出某項關鍵設備的供應商。下列哪一項公開證據，最能支持這個說法？

opts.en: Its gross margin was very high in the most recent boom year
opts.zh: 它在最近一個景氣好的年度毛利率非常高

opts.en: Its customers name it as a single-source dependency in their own risk-factor disclosures, and have previously funded its development programme and bought equity in it
opts.zh: 它的客戶在自己年報的風險因素段落把它列為單一來源依賴，而且過去曾經出資支持它的研發計畫、並買進它的股權

opts.en: Its own investor presentation states that it has no competitors
opts.zh: 它自己的投資人簡報寫著它沒有競爭對手

opts.en: It reports a very large order backlog
opts.zh: 它公布的訂單積壓金額非常龐大

exp.en: A supplier calling itself irreplaceable is marketing; a buyer conceding it in a legal disclosure, and paying before delivery, is evidence. High margin in a strong year is what any supplier shows - the distinguishing test is whether price holds through the customer downturn, not whether it is high at the peak. A backlog can be inflated by customers placing duplicate orders to hold a place in line. This customer-side evidence is also what separates a chokepoint from an oligopoly: an oligopolist depends on rivals staying restrained, whereas a genuine chokepoint has no rival to depend on and is instead bounded by the customer alternatives and by regulators.
exp.zh: 供應商自稱無可取代，那是行銷；客戶在法律揭露裡承認，而且在交貨前就先付錢，那才是證據。景氣好的年度毛利率高，是任何供應商都做得到的事——真正能分辨的檢驗，是價格在客戶衰退期間撐不撐得住，而不是它在高點高不高。訂單積壓則可能被客戶為了搶排隊位置而重複下單灌大。這種來自客戶端的證據，也正是鎖喉點和寡占的分界：寡占者要靠對手維持克制，真正的鎖喉點沒有對手可依靠，它的上限來自客戶的替代方案與監理機關。

q.en: A fast-growing subscription software company is adding customers every quarter. Does the CR3 and lead-time supply framework from this chapter directly explain its margin structure?
q.zh: 一家快速成長的訂閱制軟體公司每季都在增加客戶。這一課的 CR3 與前置時間供給架構，能直接解釋它的利潤結構嗎？

opts.en: Yes, because every business has physical capacity constraints somewhere
opts.zh: 能，因為每一家公司背後某個環節一定有實體產能限制

opts.en: No - near-zero marginal capacity constraints mean this framework barely applies, and demand-side moat tools do that work instead
opts.zh: 不能——邊際產能限制接近零，這套架構幾乎用不上，做這件事的是需求端的護城河工具

opts.en: Yes, but only if the company is already profitable
opts.zh: 能，但前提是這家公司已經開始獲利

opts.en: No, because software companies never face any competition
opts.zh: 不能，因為軟體公司從來不會面對競爭

exp.en: This toolkit assumes physical capacity is the binding constraint. For a software business, serving one more customer costs close to nothing, so CR3, lead time, and utilization explain almost none of its economics - the later chapters on switching costs and network effects do. Option 4 states the right conclusion for an entirely wrong reason, which is why it is worth rejecting explicitly: these businesses face intense competition, just not competition that runs through capacity.
exp.zh: 這套工具假設實體產能是限制所在。對一家軟體公司來說，多服務一個客戶幾乎不花成本，所以 CR3、前置時間、利用率幾乎解釋不了它的經濟體質——真正做這件事的是後面談轉換成本與網路效應的課。選項四結論對、理由卻完全錯，所以值得特別點名反駁：這類公司面對的競爭非常激烈，只是那個競爭不是透過產能發生的。

q.en: A shortage is widely reported and the obvious beneficiary stock is already up 150%. Is correctly identifying the shortage, by itself, a sufficient reason to buy the stock?
q.zh: 一個缺貨故事已經廣為人知，明顯受惠的股票也已經漲了 150%。光是正確找出這個缺貨，就足以構成買進這檔股票的理由嗎？

opts.en: Yes, a real shortage is always a buy signal
opts.zh: 是的，真實的缺貨永遠是買進訊號

opts.en: Not necessarily - the market may already have priced the recovery in, so being right about the shortage does not mean the stock is still cheap
opts.zh: 不一定——市場可能已經把復甦定價進去了，判斷缺貨正確，不代表股票現在還便宜

opts.en: Yes, because shortages always last exactly as long as the lead time and never get priced early
opts.zh: 是的，因為缺貨一定會撐滿整個前置時間，而且市場不會提前定價

opts.en: No, because shortages reported in the news are never real
opts.zh: 不是，被新聞報導出來的缺貨都不是真的

exp.en: A correct industry read and a cheap stock are two separate claims. A shortage that is common knowledge, with the beneficiary already up several-fold, can be entirely correctly identified and still be an unattractive entry point. Option 4 overcorrects into a different error: visibility does not make a shortage fake, it makes it closer to its own expiry date.
exp.zh: 判斷產業正確，跟股票便宜，是兩件不同的事。一個已經眾所皆知、受惠股也漲了好幾倍的缺貨，可能完全判斷正確，卻早就不是一個有吸引力的進場點。選項四則是矯枉過正成另一種錯誤：一個缺貨被看見，不會讓它變成假的，只會讓它離自己的到期日更近。

q.en: What question does profit-pool analysis primarily answer?
q.zh: 利潤池分析主要回答的是哪個問題？

opts.en: How big is the industry's total market capitalization
opts.zh: 這個產業的總市值有多大

opts.en: Whether the stock is cheap or expensive right now
opts.zh: 這檔股票現在貴不貴

opts.en: Across the entire value chain, where does the money actually end up
opts.zh: 整條價值鏈裡，錢實際留在誰的口袋

opts.en: How fast the industry is growing
opts.zh: 這個產業成長多快

exp.en: Profit-pool analysis is about distribution across a chain, not size, valuation, or growth rate — those are separate questions covered in other lessons.
exp.zh: 利潤池分析談的是利潤在鏈上的分布，不是規模、估值或成長率——這些是這門課其他課要回答的問題。

q.en: Company A holds 35% of an industry's total revenue and is the largest player by that measure. Company B holds only 8% of revenue but its gross margin is three times A's, and it is nearly the only supplier able to reliably mass-produce one critical process step everyone else needs. Where is the profit pool more likely concentrated?
q.zh: A公司握有某產業35%的總營收，是按這個指標排名第一的龍頭；B公司只占營收8%，毛利率卻是A的三倍，而且B幾乎是唯一能穩定量產某道所有人都需要的關鍵製程的供應商。你認為利潤池較可能集中在哪家？

opts.en: A, because it has the largest revenue share
opts.zh: A，因為它的營收占比最大

opts.en: B, because a genuine bottleneck usually captures a disproportionate share of profit regardless of revenue size
opts.zh: B，因為真正的瓶頸通常會拿走與營收規模不成比例的利潤

opts.en: They split the pool evenly, since revenue and profit pool always move together
opts.zh: 兩家平分，因為營收占比和利潤池必然同向變動

opts.en: Impossible to tell without knowing the price-earnings ratio
opts.zh: 沒辦法判斷，需要先看本益比

exp.en: Revenue share does not determine profit-pool share. A step controlling a genuine bottleneck — here signaled by near-sole ability to supply a required process step — routinely captures outsized dollar profit relative to its own revenue size.
exp.zh: 營收占比不能決定利潤池占比。掌握真正瓶頸的環節——這裡的訊號是幾乎唯一能供應必要製程步驟——經常會拿走與自身營收規模不成比例的美元利潤。

q.en: A memory-chip industry has only three major producers controlling about 95% of global supply. Does this guarantee the industry's profit pool is stable through the cycle?
q.zh: 某記憶體產業只有三大廠掌控全球約95%的供給。這是否代表這個產業的利潤池在景氣循環中會很穩定？

opts.en: Yes, three suppliers cannot meaningfully undercut each other on price
opts.zh: 是，三家供應商不太可能真的互相削價

opts.en: Yes, because a small number of sellers legally cannot compete on price
opts.zh: 是，因為賣家數量少在法律上不能打價格戰

opts.en: No, because a concentrated supply side always implies a shortage
opts.zh: 不一定，因為供給集中一定代表短缺

opts.en: No — if the product is undifferentiated, the three can still slash prices against each other in a downturn
opts.zh: 不一定——如果產品沒有差異化，三家在景氣下行時照樣會互砍價格

exp.en: Few sellers is necessary but not sufficient for pricing power. If the product itself is fungible, buyers can switch between the few suppliers freely, and the industry can still crash on price — the memory-chip cycle is the standard real-world case.
exp.zh: 賣家數量少是訂價權的必要條件，但不是充分條件。如果產品本身可以互換，買方在少數幾家供應商之間轉單幾乎沒有成本，這個產業照樣可能在價格上崩跌——記憶體晶片的循環就是最標準的現實案例。

q.en: What does purity mean in profit-pool analysis?
q.zh: 在利潤池分析裡，「純度」指的是什麼？

opts.en: The share of a company's total revenue attributable to the specific industry theme being researched
opts.zh: 公司總營收裡，可歸因於你正在研究的產業題材的比例

opts.en: How clean a company's gross margin looks on paper
opts.zh: 公司毛利率在報表上看起來有多乾淨

opts.en: The ratio of a company's debt to its total assets
opts.zh: 公司負債占總資產的比例

opts.en: How volatile a company's stock price is
opts.zh: 公司股價的波動程度

exp.en: Purity is a simple derivation: theme-related segment revenue divided by total company revenue — not a debt ratio, not volatility, not a general impression of margin quality.
exp.zh: 純度是一個簡單的推導：與題材相關的分部營收除以公司總營收——不是負債比率，不是波動度，也不是對毛利率好壞的籠統印象。

q.en: A stock has rallied hard because the market has crowned it a pure play on a hot theme. Checking the annual report, you find only 22% of its revenue is actually tied to that theme; the rest comes from an unrelated legacy business. What is the correct read?
q.zh: 某檔股票因為被市場封為某熱門題材的純概念股而大漲。你查年報後發現，只有22%的營收真正和這個題材相關，其餘78%來自不相關的舊業務。正確的判斷是什麼？

opts.en: It does not matter, since the narrative is compelling enough on its own
opts.zh: 沒差，反正故事夠吸引人就好

opts.en: Low purity automatically means the company is poorly run
opts.zh: 純度低就代表這家公司體質不好

opts.en: Purity is irrelevant once a stock starts rallying
opts.zh: 股票一旦開始上漲，純度就不重要了

opts.en: The stock's actual exposure to the theme is far lower than the pricing implies, and the rally should be re-examined against that gap
opts.zh: 這檔股票對題材的真實曝險遠低於股價所暗示的程度，應該用這個落差重新檢視這波漲勢是否合理

exp.en: Low purity does not by itself say anything about the quality of the legacy business — it says the market may be pricing in far more thematic exposure than actually exists, which is exactly the gap an analyst should flag and investigate.
exp.zh: 純度低本身並不代表舊業務的體質不好——它代表市場可能把遠比實際存在還多的題材曝險算進了股價，這正是分析者該點出來、進一步查證的落差。

q.en: Which of the following is a signal that a profit pool is migrating?
q.zh: 以下哪一個是利潤池正在遷移的訊號？

opts.en: A step's operating margin has been flat for five straight years
opts.zh: 某環節的營益率連續五年維持平盤

opts.en: A large customer starts designing or building in-house what it used to buy from a supplier
opts.zh: 大客戶開始自行設計或自製原本向供應商採購的東西

opts.en: The industry leader's stock price hits an all-time high
opts.zh: 產業龍頭的股價創下歷史新高

opts.en: The industry leader's revenue hits a new record
opts.zh: 產業龍頭的營收創下新高紀錄

exp.en: A credible in-house self-supply threat from a customer is a leading signal that leverage — and eventually profit — is shifting away from the incumbent supplier, well before revenue actually moves.
exp.zh: 客戶端出現可信的自製威脅，是籌碼、最終也是利潤正在從現有供應商身上移開的領先訊號，而且早於營收真正發生變化。

q.en: Company C posts a net margin of only 2.5%, far below its industry's 15% average, but it needs almost no inventory, collects receivables extremely fast, and spends very little on capital expenditure. How should you read its position in the profit pool?
q.zh: C公司淨利率只有2.5%，遠低於產業平均的15%，但它幾乎不需要庫存、應收帳款收現極快、資本支出也很低。你該怎麼判斷它在利潤池裡的位置？

opts.en: Low net margin means it captures very little of the pool — dismiss it immediately
opts.zh: 淨利率低就代表它在利潤池裡拿到的很少，可以直接排除

opts.en: A low margin always signals a weak competitive position with no exceptions
opts.zh: 淨利率低就一定代表競爭地位差，沒有例外

opts.en: Margin is only half the picture — check how much profit it turns from each dollar of capital, since fast turnover can still produce strong capital returns
opts.zh: 淨利率只是故事的一半，還要看它每一塊資本能轉出多少利潤，快速周轉照樣可能換來不錯的資本報酬

opts.en: A company with such a low margin is not worth researching further
opts.zh: 淨利率這麼低的公司不值得再研究

exp.en: A thin margin combined with very low capital needs can still produce a strong profit-per-capital outcome — margin percentage alone never settles the question of whether a step is a good business.
exp.zh: 薄利搭配極低的資本需求，仍然可能換來不錯的資本報酬——單看淨利率百分比永遠沒辦法斷定一個環節是不是好生意。

q.en: A four-step chain has step X generating 45% of total industry revenue at a 4% operating margin, and step Y generating only 12% of revenue at a 38% operating margin. Before doing the full calculation, what is the correct first move to compare their profit-pool shares?
q.zh: 某四環節產業鏈中，X環節占全產業營收45%、營益率僅4%；Y環節只占營收12%、營益率高達38%。在做完整計算之前，正確的第一步該怎麼比較兩者的利潤池份額？

opts.en: Compare the two revenue-share percentages directly
opts.zh: 直接比較兩者的營收占比百分比

opts.en: Compare the two operating-margin percentages directly
opts.zh: 直接比較兩者的營益率百分比

opts.en: Multiply each step's revenue by its own margin to estimate dollar operating profit for each, then compare those dollar figures
opts.zh: 把各自的營收乘以各自的營益率，估算出各自的美元營業利益，再比較這兩個美元數字

opts.en: Assume they are roughly equal since one leads on revenue and the other leads on margin
opts.zh: 假設兩者大致相等，因為一個營收領先、一個毛利率領先

exp.en: Neither revenue share nor margin alone answers a dollar-pool question — you must convert each into a dollar figure (revenue x margin) before any comparison means anything.
exp.zh: 單看營收占比或單看毛利率百分比，都無法回答美元利潤池的問題——必須先把兩者都換算成美元金額（營收×營益率），比較才有意義。

q.en: In the capital cycle mechanism, what typically happens directly after an industry earns returns well above its cost of capital for a sustained period?
q.zh: 在資本週期機制裡，當一個產業持續一段時間賺到明顯高於資金成本的報酬之後，接下來通常會發生什麼？

opts.en: Capital flows in from incumbents, new entrants, and lenders until capacity eventually rises and returns compress.
opts.zh: 既有廠商、新進者與放款方的資本開始湧入，直到產能終於增加，報酬被壓縮。

opts.en: Returns tend to stay elevated indefinitely because the market has already priced in the good news.
opts.zh: 報酬往往會無限期維持在高檔，因為市場早就把好消息定價進去了。

opts.en: Demand collapses first, which is what eventually brings returns back down.
opts.zh: 需求會先崩潰，這才是最終把報酬打下來的原因。

opts.en: Regulators typically intervene to cap the excess returns before capital can respond.
opts.zh: 監管機關通常會出手，在資本回應之前就先設下超額報酬的上限。

exp.en: The correction in a capital-intensive industry is driven by capital responding to the attractive return, not by demand collapsing or regulators stepping in — those can happen but are not the core mechanism this lesson describes.
exp.zh: 資本密集型產業的修正，是由資本對誘人報酬做出回應所驅動的，不是需求先崩潰，也不是監管機關出手介入——這些事情可能發生，但不是這一課講的核心機制。

q.en: An industry shows: capex/depreciation climbing from 1.2x to 2.9x over two years, ROIC-minus-WACC spread widening from +5pp to +38pp, and new-capacity lead time shortening as producers rush smaller, faster expansions. Which phase is this?
q.zh: 一個產業呈現：資本支出／折舊比在兩年內從1.2倍爬到2.9倍，ROIC 減 WACC 的利差從+5pp擴大到+38pp，而新產能前置時間因為生產者搶快、改用更小更快的擴產方式而正在縮短。這是哪個階段？

opts.en: Phase I, trough — capital is exiting.
opts.zh: 第一階段，谷底——資本正在退出。

opts.en: Phase II, shortage with capital flooding in.
opts.zh: 第二階段，短缺加上資金瘋狂湧入。

opts.en: Phase IV, oversupply — returns are collapsing.
opts.zh: 第四階段，供給過剩——報酬正在崩跌。

opts.en: This pattern cannot be classified without knowing the exact WACC figure.
opts.zh: 沒有精確的 WACC 數字就無法分類這個型態。

exp.en: All three proxies point the same direction — rising capex/depreciation, a widening positive spread, and a shortening lead time as producers race to expand — which is the textbook signature of Phase II. The fact that returns still look spectacular is exactly what makes this phase easy to misread as safe.
exp.zh: 三個代理指標全部指向同一個方向——資本支出／折舊比上升、正利差擴大、前置時間因為生產者搶快擴產而縮短——這正是第二階段的教科書型態。表面報酬看起來還很驚人，正是這個階段最容易被誤讀成安全的原因。

q.en: You find that capex/depreciation is falling for an industry, but the ROIC-minus-WACC spread just spiked sharply this quarter due to a one-off asset sale, and lead-time data is unavailable. What is the correct next step?
q.zh: 你發現一個產業的資本支出／折舊比正在下降，但 ROIC 減 WACC 的利差本季因為一次性資產出售而急遽飆升，而前置時間資料又找不到。正確的下一步是什麼？

opts.en: Call it Phase II immediately, since the spread spike is the strongest of the three proxies.
opts.zh: 馬上判為第二階段，因為利差飆升是三個指標裡最強的訊號。

opts.en: Do not force a phase call yet — the proxies disagree and the one that looks strongest is contaminated by a one-off item.
opts.zh: 先不要硬下階段判斷——指標彼此不一致，而且看起來最強的那個指標被一次性項目污染了。

opts.en: Average the two available proxies to get a blended phase estimate.
opts.zh: 把兩個可用的指標平均起來，算出一個混合的階段估計值。

opts.en: Assume the lead-time proxy would confirm Phase II if it were available.
opts.zh: 假設如果前置時間資料存在，它會確認是第二階段。

exp.en: Falling capex/depreciation and a spread spike point in opposite directions, and the spread number is explicitly flagged as distorted by a one-off item — this is exactly the situation the two-of-three corroboration rule exists to catch. Averaging or assuming the missing proxy agrees both smuggle back in the single-indicator mistake the rule is designed to prevent.
exp.zh: 下降的資本支出／折舊比和飆升的利差彼此矛盾，而且利差數字已經明確被標註為受一次性項目扭曲——這正是「兩個一致」原則存在的目的，就是要抓住這種情況。無論是把兩個指標平均，或假設缺失的那個指標會一致，其實都是偷偷把單一指標判斷的錯誤又帶回來。

q.en: Why is supply generally easier to forecast than demand in a capital-intensive industry?
q.zh: 為什麼在資本密集型產業裡，供給通常比需求更容易預測？

opts.en: Because supply data is public information already substantially locked in through committed capex, permits and construction schedules, while demand depends on future consumer and customer behavior that cannot be directly observed.
opts.zh: 因為供給的資料多半已經公開，而且透過已核准的資本支出、許可與建置時程被大幅鎖定，而需求則取決於未來消費者與客戶的行為，這是無法直接觀察到的。

opts.en: Because regulators require companies to publish exact production forecasts, while demand forecasts are unregulated.
opts.zh: 因為監管機關要求公司公布精確的產量預測，而需求預測不受監管。

opts.en: Because supply never changes once a factory is built, so there is nothing left to forecast.
opts.zh: 因為工廠蓋好之後供給就不會再變，所以根本沒什麼好預測的。

opts.en: Because demand is always more volatile than supply in every industry, by definition.
opts.zh: 因為在任何產業裡，需求依定義永遠比供給更不穩定。

exp.en: The core reason is informational, not regulatory or definitional: committed capital spending, permits, and construction schedules are close to facts you can look up, while future demand depends on unobservable behavior. Supply absolutely can and does change after a factory is built (through utilization, expansion, or exit) — the point is not that it is fixed, but that its trajectory is more knowable in advance.
exp.zh: 核心原因是資訊面的，不是監管或定義上的：已投入的資本支出、許可、建置時程，接近是查得到的事實，而未來需求則取決於無法觀察的行為。供給在工廠蓋好之後當然還是會變（透過利用率、擴產或退出），重點不是它固定不變，而是它的走勢比較能提前掌握。

q.en: A management team says on an earnings call, "We do not see any credible new competitors entering this market." Should this statement, on its own, count as capital-cycle evidence that the industry is not in Phase II?
q.zh: 一家公司的管理層在法說會上說：「我們看不到有任何可信的新競爭者要進入這個市場。」這句話本身，能不能算是資本週期的證據，證明這個產業不在第二階段？

opts.en: Yes — management has the best visibility into competitive dynamics, so their statement should be trusted directly.
opts.zh: 能——管理層對競爭動態的了解最深入，他們的說法應該直接被信任。

opts.en: No — it is a narrative statement with an incentive to sound confident, and should be checked against the actual capex/depreciation, ROIC-WACC spread, and lead-time data before it changes your phase call.
opts.zh: 不能——這是一句帶有讓自己聽起來有信心誘因的敘事性發言，應該拿去跟實際的資本支出／折舊比、ROIC-WACC 利差、前置時間資料交叉核對，才能改變你的階段判斷。

opts.en: Yes, but only if the company is the market leader.
opts.zh: 能，但只有在這家公司是市場龍頭時才算。

opts.en: No, because management statements are always deliberately false.
opts.zh: 不能，因為管理層的發言永遠是刻意造假的。

exp.en: This lesson explicitly treats management commentary on demand and competition as narrative, not evidence, precisely because management has every incentive to sound confident regardless of what they privately expect. The correct move is not to assume they are lying, but to require the quantitative proxies before letting a statement like this move your phase call.
exp.zh: 這一課明確把管理層對需求與競爭的評論，當成敘事而不是證據，原因正是管理層無論私底下怎麼想，都有充分誘因把話講得信心滿滿。正確的做法不是假設他們在說謊，而是要求量化代理指標的佐證，才能讓這種發言真的改變你的階段判斷。

q.en: A subscription software company shows almost no relationship between its ROIC and its capital spending — it can add server and staff capacity within a single quarter. How useful is the capital-cycle framework for judging this company's forward returns?
q.zh: 一家訂閱制軟體公司的 ROIC 跟資本支出幾乎看不出關聯——它可以在單一季度內就加出伺服器與人力產能。資本週期框架對判斷這家公司未來的報酬有多大用處？

opts.en: Very useful — every industry follows the same capital cycle regardless of capital intensity.
opts.zh: 非常有用——不管資本密集度多高，每個產業都遵循同一套資本週期。

opts.en: Not very useful — with near-zero lead time and low capital intensity, the framework's core mechanism barely applies, and other tools should carry more weight.
opts.zh: 不太有用——在前置時間趨近於零、資本密集度又低的情況下，這套框架的核心機制幾乎不適用，應該讓其他工具承擔更多份量。

opts.en: Somewhat useful, but only after converting employee headcount into an equivalent capex/depreciation ratio.
opts.zh: 還算有用，但要先把員工人數換算成等效的資本支出／折舊比才行。

opts.en: Not useful at all, because software companies never earn returns above their cost of capital.
opts.zh: 完全沒用，因為軟體公司從來不會賺到高於資金成本的報酬。

exp.en: This lesson states the boundary explicitly: the capital cycle is a strong lens where returns are tied to physical, lead-time-heavy capacity, and a weak one where capacity can be added in weeks or months. Trying to force the same mechanical read onto an asset-light business — including artificially converting headcount into a capex ratio — mostly produces noise rather than insight.
exp.zh: 這一課明確講了邊界：資本週期在報酬與實體、前置時間長的產能綁在一起時是一把強尺，在產能可以在幾週或幾個月內加出來時是一把弱尺。硬要把同一套機械式判讀套到資產輕的生意上——包括刻意把人數換算成資本支出比率——多半只會產生雜訊，而不是洞見。

q.en: Why does this lesson argue that a verified, visible shortage with capital flooding in is one of the most dangerous entry points, rather than one of the safest?
q.zh: 為什麼這一課主張一個已驗證、看得見的短缺加上資金瘋狂湧入，是最危險的進場點之一，而不是最安全的進場點之一？

opts.en: Because shortages are almost always fabricated by companies to inflate their stock price.
opts.zh: 因為短缺幾乎都是公司為了拉高股價而捏造出來的。

opts.en: Because a shortage visible enough for you to confirm it is also visible enough for the market to have already priced it in, while the capital already committed to ending the shortage is the leading indicator of the glut that follows.
opts.zh: 因為一個清楚到你能確認的短缺，也清楚到市場早就已經把它定價進去，而已經投入來終結這個短缺的資本，正是接下來過剩產能的領先指標。

opts.en: Because shortages always resolve within a single quarter, too fast for investors to react.
opts.zh: 因為短缺總是在單一季度內就解決，快到投資人根本來不及反應。

opts.en: Because industries in shortage are legally required to disclose it, eliminating any informational edge.
opts.zh: 因為處於短缺的產業依法必須揭露這件事，讓資訊優勢消失。

exp.en: The double bind is the point: the shortage is real, but its visibility means it is priced, and the same conditions that make it exciting enough to notice are what pull in the capital that eventually ends it. A retrospective look at a large batch of calls made specifically in this cell found a win rate well under a third, precisely because the physical read was often correct while the pricing and capital-response read was missing.
exp.zh: 這個雙重束縛正是重點：短缺是真的，但它的能見度代表已經被定價，而讓它精彩到被注意到的那些條件，正是把最終終結它的資本吸引進來的原因。事後回頭檢視一大批專門在這一格做出的判斷，發現命中率遠低於三分之一，原因正是實體面的判讀往往是對的，但定價與資本回應的判讀漏掉了。

q.en: Crude oil prices spike sharply after a sudden, unplanned outage at a major producing region, with no accompanying change in the industry's capex/depreciation ratio, ROIC-WACC spread trend, or lead-time data. Should this price spike, on its own, be read as evidence of a capital-cycle phase change?
q.zh: 某個主要產油地區突然發生非計畫性的供應中斷，導致原油價格急遽飆升，但產業的資本支出／折舊比、ROIC-WACC 利差走勢、前置時間資料都沒有跟著變動。這個價格飆升，單獨能不能被解讀成資本週期階段轉換的證據？

opts.en: Yes — any sharp price spike is definitionally a Phase II signal.
opts.zh: 能——任何急遽的價格飆升，依定義就是第二階段訊號。

opts.en: No — a price spike driven by a short-term, non-capital-related disruption is a different animal from a capital-cycle phase change, and should not be read as one without the underlying proxies also moving.
opts.zh: 不能——由短期、與資本無關的中斷所驅動的價格飆升，跟資本週期階段轉換是不同的東西，除非底層代理指標也一起變動，否則不該被解讀成階段轉換。

opts.en: Yes, because oil is a commodity and all commodity price moves reflect capital-cycle phases by definition.
opts.zh: 能，因為石油是大宗商品，所有大宗商品的價格變動依定義都反映資本週期階段。

opts.en: No, because price data should never be used anywhere in capital-cycle analysis.
opts.zh: 不能，因為價格資料絕對不該用在資本週期分析的任何地方。

exp.en: The whole point of anchoring the framework in capex/depreciation, the ROIC-WACC spread, and lead time is to avoid mistaking a short-lived, supply-disruption-driven price move for the slower, capital-driven cycle this lesson describes. A genuine phase change should eventually show up in the proxies too, once the disruption resolves and capital responds one way or another — a one-off outage with no capital response is not that.
exp.zh: 把整套框架錨定在資本支出／折舊比、ROIC-WACC 利差和前置時間上，用意正是要避免把一次短暫、由供應中斷驅動的價格波動，誤認成這一課講的那種較慢、由資本驅動的循環。一次真正的階段轉換，最終也應該會反映在這些代理指標上——等中斷解除、資本以某種方式做出回應之後；一次沒有伴隨資本回應的單次意外中斷，並不是那回事。

q.en: What is the defining test for whether a new product is a genuine substitution threat rather than ordinary competition?
q.zh: 判斷一個新產品是不是真正的替代威脅，而不只是一般競爭，關鍵測試是什麼？

opts.en: Whether it uses newer technology
opts.zh: 它有沒有用更新的技術

opts.en: Whether it completes the same underlying job through a different mechanism at a switching cost low enough to matter
opts.zh: 它有沒有用不同機制完成同一個底層工作，而且轉換成本低到會構成影響

opts.en: Whether it is cheaper
opts.zh: 它有沒有比較便宜

exp.en: Newer technology and lower price can both be true of an ordinary same-architecture competitor. The test is the job plus the mechanism plus switching cost together — a substitute wins by doing the job a different way, not just doing the same thing better.
exp.zh: 更新的技術跟更便宜的價格，一般同架構的競爭對手也可能都符合。測試看的是工作本身加上機制加上轉換成本三者合在一起——替代品是用不同方式完成同一個工作而勝出，不是只把同一件事做得更好。

q.en: A regional bus company sees ride-hailing apps grow ridership sharply in its market and worries about substitution. What should it check first?
q.zh: 一家地區巴士公司看到叫車 App 在自己的市場搭乘量大幅成長，開始擔心被替代。它該先查什麼？

opts.en: Whether ride-hailing pricing has historically been reliant on investor subsidy, and whether it is drawing riders from bus or mostly from private car and taxi
opts.zh: 叫車 App 的定價過去是否依賴投資人補貼，以及它搶的客源主要是巴士，還是私家車與計程車

opts.en: Whether ride-hailing apps have better technology
opts.zh: 叫車 App 的技術是否比較好

opts.en: Whether the bus company should build its own app
opts.zh: 巴士公司要不要自己做一個 App

exp.en: Ride-hailing growth against a subsidized, below-cost price is not the same signal as growth at a sustainable price, and if the new riders are mostly former car and taxi users rather than former bus riders, the job being substituted may not be the bus's job at all.
exp.zh: 在補貼、低於成本的價格下成長，跟在可持續價格下成長，是完全不同的訊號；而如果新增乘客大多是原本開車或搭計程車的人、不是原本搭巴士的人，那被替代的可能根本不是巴士這個工作。

q.en: A supplier earns unusually high margins from one customer that accounts for over half its revenue. Under the framework in this lesson, what should this raise as a question?
q.zh: 一家供應商從一個占其營收超過一半的客戶身上賺取異常高的毛利。依照這一課的框架，這應該引出什麼問題？

opts.en: Whether this margin and concentration together are building the customer's case for eventually building the capability in-house
opts.zh: 這樣的毛利加上集中度，是不是正在替客戶累積將來自己做的理由

opts.en: Nothing, high margin with a large customer is simply a strong business
opts.zh: 沒什麼問題，跟大客戶做出高毛利本來就是一門好生意

opts.en: Whether the supplier should raise prices further
opts.zh: 供應商要不要再進一步漲價

exp.en: High margin plus high concentration is the setup this lesson calls counterintuitive: it looks like strength but is exactly the condition that makes customer in-house build economically attractive, since the fatter the margin being paid out, the larger the saving from bringing it in-house.
exp.zh: 高毛利加上高集中度，正是這一課點出的反直覺情境：它看起來是優勢，但恰好就是讓客戶自研在經濟上變得划算的條件——付出去的毛利愈肥，收回自己做能省下的錢就愈多。

q.en: An industry newsletter reports a proposed regulation that would ban a widely used component within two years. What should an analyst check before treating this as a confirmed substitution trigger?
q.zh: 一份產業電子報報導一項擬議法規，將在兩年內禁用一個廣泛使用的零組件。分析者在把這件事當成確認的替代觸發點之前，應該先查什麼？

opts.en: The proposal's actual effective date, enforcement mechanism, and how politically durable the underlying coalition behind it is
opts.zh: 這項提案實際的生效日期、執行機制，以及背後推動的政治聯盟有多穩固

opts.en: Nothing, a regulatory headline is sufficient to act on
opts.zh: 不用查，法規標題本身就足以據此行動

opts.en: Only whether the affected companies have issued a statement
opts.zh: 只需要查受影響公司有沒有發過聲明

exp.en: Policy-driven substitution moves on a legislative and enforcement clock that is frequently slower, weaker, or more reversible than a headline suggests. The check is the same as for any load-bearing fact: verify the specific mechanism and its durability, not the announcement.
exp.zh: 由政策驅動的替代，是照著立法與執法的時鐘走的，而這個時鐘往往比標題給人的印象更慢、更弱，或更容易被推翻。這裡的查證方式跟任何承重事實一樣：驗證具體的執行機制與它的穩固程度，而不是驗證那則新聞標題。

q.en: A cheaper alternative technology currently performs far worse than the incumbent on every metric that matters to customers today. What is the strongest reason this could still be dismissed too early?
q.zh: 一個更便宜的替代技術，目前在所有客戶在意的指標上都遠遠不如現有技術。太早把它打發掉，最站得住腳的理由是什麼？

opts.en: The comparison that matters is the rate of improvement of each side over the relevant time horizon, not where each stands today
opts.zh: 真正重要的比較，是雙方在相關時間長度內的改善速度，不是雙方現在站在哪裡

opts.en: Cheaper technology always wins eventually regardless of performance
opts.zh: 更便宜的技術到最後一定會贏，不管性能如何

opts.en: Incumbents never improve their own technology in response
opts.zh: 在位者面對挑戰時從不改善自己的技術

exp.en: A large current performance gap says little on its own; what matters is whether the challenger's improvement rate, extended forward, crosses the incumbent's cost or performance line inside the time horizon that matters for the position being evaluated.
exp.zh: 現在的性能差距有多大，本身能說明的不多；重點是把挑戰者的改善速度往前拉，看它會不會在你這個部位在意的時間長度內，跨過在位者的成本或性能線。

q.en: An analyst finishes a mechanical scan and reports that no material substitution threat was found for a company. Is this an acceptable outcome?
q.zh: 一位分析者跑完機械掃描，回報沒有找到這家公司的實質替代威脅。這是一個可以接受的結果嗎？

opts.en: No, a scan must always surface at least one threat to be considered complete
opts.zh: 不行，掃描一定要找出至少一個威脅才算完整

opts.en: Yes, provided the candidate list and disposition for each item were actually documented, with a named signal that would reopen the question
opts.zh: 可以，前提是候選清單與每一項的處置真的有留下紀錄，並點名一個會重新打開這個問題的訊號

opts.en: No, because every industry always has a real substitution threat somewhere
opts.zh: 不行，因為每個產業一定都有一個真實的替代威脅存在

exp.en: A documented negative result is a legitimate output of the scan — the failure mode this lesson warns about is skipping the scan and producing silence, not the scan honestly finding nothing.
exp.zh: 有紀錄的否定結果，是這個掃描一個正當的產出——這一課警告的失敗模式，是跳過掃描而只留下沉默，不是掃描認真跑過之後誠實地什麼都沒找到。

q.en: A supplier's largest customer quietly increases hiring for chip-design roles and begins issuing design-win announcements for a category the supplier has long dominated, while the supplier's revenue from that customer has not yet declined. What is the correct read?
q.zh: 一家供應商的最大客戶悄悄增加晶片設計相關職位的招募，並開始針對供應商長期主導的品類發布設計得標公告，而供應商從這個客戶身上的營收目前還沒有下滑。正確的解讀是什麼？

opts.en: No action needed until the revenue actually declines
opts.zh: 不需要做任何事，等營收真的下滑再說

opts.en: Hiring and design-win activity are typically leading signals of a customer in-house build that show up months before any revenue impact — this belongs on the tracked-metric list now
opts.zh: 招募與設計得標動態通常是客戶自研的領先訊號，會比營收受影響早好幾個月出現——現在就該把它列進追蹤指標

opts.en: This is unrelated to substitution since the supplier and the new effort use the same manufacturing process
opts.zh: 這跟替代無關，因為供應商跟這個新動作用的是同一套製造流程

exp.en: Revenue is a lagging number in this kind of substitution. Hiring and design-win announcements are the earliest visible signal, consistent with the customer-in-house pattern described earlier in this lesson, and using the same underlying manufacturing process does not make it less of a substitution threat to the original supplier's order flow.
exp.zh: 在這類替代情境裡，營收是落後指標。招募與設計得標公告是最早能看到的訊號，符合這一課前面講過的客戶自研模式；用同一套底層製造流程，並不會讓它對原供應商訂單的替代威脅變得比較小。

q.en: In Costco's business model as described in this lesson, which of the following best describes the actual profit engine?
q.zh: 照這一課的分析，好市多商業模式真正的利益引擎，最貼切的描述是什麼？

opts.en: A high markup on merchandise sold in warehouses
opts.zh: 賣場商品的高加價

opts.en: Real estate appreciation on the warehouse properties
opts.zh: 賣場不動產的增值

opts.en: Prepaid membership fees renewed at a high rate, funding a merchandise operation run near cost
opts.zh: 預收、且高續卡率的會員費，資助一個貼著成本經營的商品營運

opts.en: Store-brand product margins alone
opts.zh: 單靠自有品牌商品的利益率

exp.en: The markup cap of roughly 14% makes merchandise margin thin by design, not by accident, so the high-markup answer describes exactly the surface number the opening case warned against reading alone. In fiscal 2023, membership fees of about $4.6B were under 2% of revenue but supplied on the order of 55%–60% of operating income — the engine is the fee, and the cheap merchandise is what keeps the fee worth renewing.
exp.zh: 約 14% 的加價上限，讓商品毛利薄是刻意設計、不是意外，所以「賣場商品的高加價」正是開場案例提醒過、不能單獨解讀的表面數字。2023 財年約 46 億美元的會員費不到營收的 2%，卻貢獻了約當五成五到六成的營業利益——引擎是那筆會員費，便宜的商品則是讓這筆費用值得續下去的原因。

q.en: A subscription company reports ARPU of $40/month, 65% gross margin, monthly churn of 4%, and CAC of $350. Approximately what is its LTV/CAC ratio, and how should that number be read?
q.zh: 一家訂閱制公司月 ARPU 40 美元、毛利率 65%、月流失率 4%、CAC 350 美元。它的 LTV/CAC 大約是多少，這個數字又該怎麼解讀？

opts.en: About 1.9x, below the roughly 3x heuristic — a reason to check payback period and cohort trends, not an automatic disqualifier
opts.zh: 約 1.9 倍，低於約 3 倍的經驗法則——這是去查回本期與世代留存趨勢的理由，不是自動出局

opts.en: About 1.9x, comfortably above the typical heuristic threshold
opts.zh: 約 1.9 倍，穩穩超過常見的經驗法則門檻

opts.en: About 6x, a strong reading
opts.zh: 約 6 倍，是不錯的水準

opts.en: Cannot be estimated from the data given
opts.zh: 用給定的資料無法估算

exp.en: LTV ≈ ARPU × gross margin ÷ churn = 40 × 0.65 ÷ 0.04 = $650; LTV/CAC = 650 ÷ 350 ≈ 1.9x. The answer calling 1.9x comfortably above the threshold gets the arithmetic right and the reading backwards. And because that formula is undiscounted and infinite-horizon, the honest number over a three-year window is lower still, which is why the response is scrutiny rather than a verdict.
exp.zh: LTV ≈ ARPU × 毛利率 ÷ 流失率 ＝ 40 × 0.65 ÷ 0.04 ＝ 650 美元；LTV/CAC ＝ 650 ÷ 350 ≈ 1.9 倍。說 1.9 倍「穩穩超過門檻」的那個答案，算式對、解讀反了。而且這個公式沒有折現、又假設無限期，改用三年窗口誠實地重算會更低——所以正確的反應是進一步查證，不是直接下判決。

q.en: A company's contribution margin is $40M and its base operating income is $8M. If revenue grows 12% this year, roughly what growth rate should be expected in operating income, all else equal?
q.zh: 一家公司貢獻邊際 4,000 萬美元、基準營業利益 800 萬美元。若今年營收成長 12%，在其他條件不變下，營業利益大約會成長多少？

opts.en: About 12%
About 24%
About 60%
Cannot be determined from this data
opts.zh: 用這些資料無法判斷

exp.en: Degree of operating leverage ≈ contribution margin ÷ base operating income = 40 ÷ 8 = 5x, so operating income growth ≈ 12% × 5 = 60%. Answering 12% assumes there are no fixed costs at all, which would require contribution margin and operating income to be the same number.
exp.zh: 營業槓桿係數 ≈ 貢獻邊際 ÷ 基準營業利益 ＝ 40 ÷ 8 ＝ 5 倍，所以營業利益成長率 ≈ 12% × 5 ＝ 60%。答 12% 等於假設完全沒有固定成本，那要貢獻邊際與營業利益是同一個數字才成立。

q.en: A company's annual filing shows capital expenditure at just 2% of revenue, which management highlights as evidence of an asset-light model. Which single piece of additional disclosure would most directly test that claim?
q.zh: 一家公司年報顯示資本支出僅佔營收 2%，經營層將此列為輕資產模式的證據。要最直接驗證這個說法，該優先查哪一項揭露？

opts.en: The trailing five-year revenue CAGR
opts.zh: 過去五年的營收年複合成長率

opts.en: Marketing spend as a percentage of revenue
opts.zh: 行銷支出佔營收比

opts.en: The number of full-time employees
opts.zh: 全職員工人數

opts.en: The weighted-average remaining term and total value of operating lease liabilities
opts.zh: 營業租賃負債的加權平均剩餘年限與總金額

exp.en: Low capex coexists comfortably with real capital intensity that has simply moved onto the balance sheet as a long-dated lease obligation — the WeWork mechanism in this lesson, where future lease commitments ran to roughly 25 times annual revenue on a term near 15 years. None of the other three disclosures says anything about where the capital commitment sits.
exp.zh: 低資本支出，完全可以跟真實的資本密集度並存，只是後者搬到資產負債表上、變成一筆長年期租賃義務——正是這一課 WeWork 的機制：未來租賃承諾約當年營收的 25 倍，租期約 15 年。另外三項揭露，都答不出資本承諾實際坐落在哪裡。

q.en: Which combination of characteristics produces a negative cash conversion cycle?
q.zh: 哪一種特徵組合，會產生負的現金循環週期？

opts.en: Long inventory lead times combined with generous customer payment terms
opts.zh: 長備貨前置期，加上給顧客寬鬆的付款條件

opts.en: Customers pay at the time of purchase, while the company pays its own suppliers on delayed terms
opts.zh: 顧客下單當下就付款，公司付供應商的條件卻是延後的

opts.en: High fixed costs combined with low variable costs
opts.zh: 高固定成本，加上低變動成本

opts.en: High customer switching costs combined with long contract terms
opts.zh: 高轉換成本，加上長合約期限

exp.en: CCC = DIO + DSO − DPO. Immediate customer payment (low DSO) plus late supplier payment (high DPO) can push the whole expression negative, so cash arrives before it must leave. Long lead times plus generous customer terms describe the opposite, cash-hungry pattern; the cost-structure and switching-cost answers are about operating leverage and stickiness, which are different questions entirely.
exp.zh: CCC ＝ DIO ＋ DSO － DPO。顧客立刻付款（DSO 低）加上晚付供應商（DPO 高），可以把整個算式推成負值，現金進來的時間早於出去的時間。長備貨前置期加上寬鬆的顧客付款條件，描述的正是相反、吃現金的那一種；成本結構與轉換成本那兩個答案講的是營業槓桿與黏著度，是完全不同的問題。

q.en: Two companies post the same operating margin this year. Company A earns it on prepaid subscription revenue with 115% net revenue retention; Company B earns it on one-time project revenue with no recurring component. Which statement is most defensible?
q.zh: 兩家公司今年的營業利益率相同。甲公司的利益率來自淨收入留存率 115% 的預收訂閱營收；乙公司則來自沒有任何重複性的一次性專案營收。哪一個說法最站得住腳？

opts.en: Company A's revenue is more forecastable, a real quality difference the market usually prices higher — but whether it is worth buying still depends on the price paid, not on quality alone
opts.zh: 甲公司的營收可預測性較高，是真實的品質差異，市場通常也會給比較高的定價——但值不值得買，仍取決於實際付出的價格，不是只看品質

opts.en: Since margins are identical, the two businesses deserve the same valuation multiple
opts.zh: 利益率既然一樣，兩家公司就該給同樣的估值倍數

opts.en: Company B is automatically the better investment because one-time revenue avoids customer concentration risk
opts.zh: 乙公司自動是比較好的投資標的，因為一次性營收沒有客戶集中風險

opts.en: Margin is the only input that matters for valuing either company
opts.zh: 利益率是評價這兩家公司唯一重要的輸入

exp.en: Predictability is a genuine quality difference and the market generally prices it, which is exactly why the higher-quality business is rarely the cheaper one. A good business is still not automatically a good stock at any price — that separate question belongs to the valuation lesson later in this course.
exp.zh: 可預測性是真實的品質差異，市場通常也會反映在定價上——這正是為什麼品質較好的那一家，很少同時是比較便宜的那一家。好生意在任何價格下都不會自動變成好股票；這個獨立的問題，屬於這門課後面估值那一課。

q.en: An investor finds a business with a clear, durable engine and an honest, rational management team, but admits they do not understand the regulatory environment it operates in well enough to know what would break it. Under the four-question threshold in this lesson, what should happen next?
q.zh: 一位投資人找到一門引擎清楚且持久、經營層也理性誠實的生意，卻承認自己看不懂它所處的法規環境，說不出具體什麼情況會讓它出問題。照這一課的四道門檻問題，接下來該怎麼做？

opts.en: Proceed, since two of the four questions were already answered favorably
opts.zh: 繼續往下走，反正四題裡已經有兩題答得不錯

opts.en: Proceed only if the price looks cheap enough
opts.zh: 只要價格夠便宜就可以繼續

opts.en: Add a fifth question about brand recognition instead
opts.zh: 改成加問第五題，問品牌知名度

opts.en: Stop — the understand-it question gates the other three; a favorable read on advantage or management cannot substitute for it
opts.zh: 停下來——理解得了這一題是其他三題的前提關卡，優勢或經營層答得好都不能替代它

exp.en: The four questions are sequential, not an average to be scored. Someone who cannot name specifically what would break a business is not in a position to judge its durability, its management, or its price honestly, because all three of those judgments rest on knowing the failure modes. The cheap-enough-price answer is the most tempting error: a low price is compensation for risk that has been identified, not for risk that has not been.
exp.zh: 這四題是依序過關，不是拿來平均打分數的。一個說不出具體什麼會讓生意出問題的人，也就沒有立場誠實評估它的持久性、經營層或價格，因為這三個判斷全都建立在知道失敗模式之上。「只要夠便宜就繼續」是最誘人的錯誤：低價是對已經被辨識出來的風險的補償，不是對還沒被辨識出來的風險的補償。

q.en: A coffee chain raises prices 8% when input costs jump 12%, and next quarter's volume falls only 2%. A discount coffee chain raises prices 8% in the same period and volume falls 15%. Which chain more likely has a moat?
q.zh: 一家連鎖咖啡店在原物料成本上漲12%時把售價調漲8%，隔季銷量只掉了2%；同期一家平價咖啡連鎖同樣調漲8%，銷量卻掉了15%。哪一家比較可能有護城河？

opts.en: The first chain — it passed the pricing-power test
opts.zh: 前者——它通過了定價權測試

opts.en: The second chain — it raised prices at the same time
opts.zh: 後者——它也在同一時間漲價了

opts.en: Neither — both raised prices, so both are equally exposed
opts.zh: 都不是——兩家都漲價，代表兩家一樣容易受影響

opts.en: Can't tell without knowing gross margin
opts.zh: 不知道毛利率就無法判斷

exp.en: A small volume drop after a real price increase is the direct pricing-power test this lesson describes — customers stayed even though it now costs more. A 15% volume drop shows customers are price-sensitive and will switch, which is the opposite signal. Both companies raising prices doesn't make them equally protected; what matters is what happened to volume afterward.
exp.zh: 漲價之後銷量只掉一點點，正是這一課講的定價權直接測試——即使變貴了，客戶還是留下來。銷量掉15%代表消費者對價格敏感、會轉單，這是相反的訊號。兩家都漲價不代表兩家一樣有保障，重點是漲價之後銷量發生了什麼事。

q.en: A used-goods marketplace grows from 1 million to 10 million users, and both matching speed and closing price improve as it grows. A hardware retail chain grows from 50 to 500 stores, and per-store procurement cost falls due to bulk buying. Which advantage better fits the definition of a network effect?
q.zh: 一家二手交易平台使用者數從100萬成長到1000萬，媒合速度與成交價都跟著變好；一家五金連鎖賣場從50家店擴張到500家，因為採購量變大，單店採購成本下降。哪一個比較符合網路效應的定義？

opts.en: The marketplace — more users make the product better for existing users
opts.zh: 二手交易平台——用戶增加讓既有用戶得到更多價值

opts.en: The hardware chain — more scale lowered costs
opts.zh: 五金賣場——規模擴大降低了成本

opts.en: Both — they're the same mechanism at different scales
opts.zh: 兩者都是——只是規模不同，機制一樣

opts.en: Neither — user count and store count alone prove nothing
opts.zh: 都不是——單看用戶數或店數本身不能證明什麼

exp.en: Network effect means value, not just cost, rises with participants — the marketplace fits because matching speed and price genuinely improve as the user base grows. The hardware chain's improvement is a cost advantage from purchasing scale, a different mechanism entirely, even though both examples show a company getting bigger.
exp.zh: 網路效應指的是「價值」而不只是「成本」隨參與者增加而提升——二手平台符合這個定義，因為媒合速度和成交價確實隨用戶數變好。五金賣場的改善來自採購規模帶來的成本優勢，是完全不同的機制，即使兩個例子都是公司規模變大。

q.en: A cloud accounting platform's customers have used it for an average of 8 years; after a 15% price hike, renewal rate dropped just 1 point. A music streaming app raised prices 10% and lost 20% of subscribers within a month. Which one's switching cost is more likely real, not just habit?
q.zh: 一款雲端會計軟體的用戶平均用了8年；調漲訂閱費15%後，續約率只掉了1個百分點。一款串流音樂App調漲10%，一個月內流失了20%的訂戶。哪一個的轉換成本比較可能是真的，而不只是慣性？

opts.en: The streaming app — its users had stuck around for years too
opts.zh: 串流App——它的用戶也黏著很多年了

opts.en: Both — long tenure alone proves switching cost in either case
opts.zh: 兩者皆是——用了很久本身就代表轉換成本

opts.en: The accounting platform — it survived a real price-increase test
opts.zh: 會計軟體——它撐過了真正的漲價測試

opts.en: Neither — a single price increase isn't enough evidence
opts.zh: 都不是——一次漲價不足以當證據

exp.en: The accounting platform passed the only test that counts — churn barely moved after a larger price increase, consistent with real data-migration and retraining costs. The streaming app's users looked loyal right up until the test happened, then a 10% hike triggered a 20% loss — exactly the pattern of habit that was never priced, not a real switching cost.
exp.zh: 會計軟體通過了唯一算數的測試——即使漲幅更大，續訂率幾乎沒動，符合真實資料搬遷與重新訓練成本的樣子。串流App的用戶在被測試之前看起來也很忠誠，結果一次10%的漲價就流失了20%——這正是「從沒被漲價測試過的慣性」的典型樣子，不是真正的轉換成本。

q.en: Two phone brands both score above 90% in consumer brand-awareness surveys. One has raised average selling price steadily for five years while holding 35%+ gross margin; the other has cut average selling price for three straight years to defend shipment volume, with margin down to 18%. Which one more likely has a real intangible-asset moat, not just awareness?
q.zh: 兩個手機品牌在消費者調查裡的知名度都超過90%。其中一家過去五年平均售價持續上升、毛利率穩定維持在35%以上；另一家為了維持出貨量，過去三年平均售價持續下滑，毛利率跌到18%。哪一家比較可能擁有真正的無形資產型護城河，而不只是知名度？

opts.en: The second — it's working harder to keep customers
opts.zh: 後者——它更努力留住客戶

opts.en: The first — pricing power sustained the margin
opts.zh: 前者——定價權讓毛利率撐住了

opts.en: Both equally — awareness is what matters, not price
opts.zh: 兩者一樣——重要的是知名度，不是價格

opts.en: Neither — margin depends on manufacturing cost, not brand
opts.zh: 都不是——毛利率是製造成本決定的，跟品牌無關

exp.en: Brand awareness is the same for both, which is exactly the point — awareness alone tells you nothing. The company that could keep raising prices while margin held is showing the actual evidence of an intangible-asset moat (pricing power); the one cutting price to defend volume is showing the opposite — its brand isn't buying it any pricing power at all.
exp.zh: 兩家的知名度一樣高，這正是重點——單看知名度什麼都看不出來。能持續漲價又守住毛利率的那家，才展現出無形資產護城河的真正證據（定價權）；靠降價維持出貨量的那家，展現的是相反的訊號——它的品牌根本沒有換來任何定價權。

q.en: A regional natural-gas distributor serves an area whose total demand can just barely cover one operator's fixed costs plus a reasonable profit. A second operator entering would push both into losses. Which moat source does this describe?
q.zh: 一家區域天然氣配送商，服務範圍的總需求量剛好只夠支撐一家業者打平固定成本並賺取合理利潤。如果第二家業者進場，雙方都會虧損。這最接近哪一種護城河來源？

opts.en: Cost advantage
opts.zh: 成本優勢

opts.en: Efficient scale
opts.zh: 有效規模

opts.en: Network effect
opts.zh: 網路效應

opts.en: Switching cost
opts.zh: 轉換成本

exp.en: This is the defining case of efficient scale: no patent, no brand, no habit — a rational second entrant simply does the arithmetic, sees the market can't profitably support two players, and stays out.
exp.zh: 這正是有效規模的定義案例：沒有專利、沒有品牌、沒有慣性——一個理性的第二家業者只是算過帳，發現這個市場撐不起兩家一起賺，於是選擇不進來。

q.en: In 2021, several ocean-shipping companies posted record profits and their stocks rallied together, driven by a global container shortage and freight-rate spike, not by any one company being harder to compete with. What does that profit surge mainly reflect?
q.zh: 2021年，多家海運公司獲利創歷史新高、股價齊漲，原因是全球缺櫃與運價暴漲，不是哪一家公司特別難被取代。這波獲利成長主要反映的是什麼？

opts.en: Their moats got wider
opts.zh: 護城河變寬了

opts.en: An industry-wide cyclical tailwind
opts.zh: 產業順風（景氣循環）

opts.en: A jump in switching costs
opts.zh: 轉換成本提高了

opts.en: Better management across the industry
opts.zh: 整個產業的管理層突然變強了

exp.en: When every player's numbers move together for the same external, industry-wide reason, that's the tailwind test described earlier in this lesson — the industry got paid well, which is not the same as any single company having a durable edge over its rivals.
exp.zh: 當所有業者的數字，都因為同一個外部、產業層級的原因同時往同一個方向移動，這正是本課前面講的順風測試——是整個產業被市場多付了錢，跟某一家公司比對手更有優勢是不同的事。

q.en: A social platform was the first mover in its category and built an early lead in users and media buzz. Two years later, a later entrant with better features and a viral invite mechanism overtook it, and the original users largely migrated. What does this best illustrate?
q.zh: 一個社群平台是所屬類別最早上線的產品，累積了先發用戶與媒體聲量。兩年後，一個功能更好、有病毒式邀請機制的後進者迅速超車，原本的用戶大量轉移過去。這說明了什麼？

opts.en: Being first automatically becomes a network-effect moat over time
opts.zh: 先進場久了自然會變成網路效應護城河

opts.en: A first-mover lead only becomes a moat if it gets converted into a real source before a challenger arrives
opts.zh: 先行者的領先，只有在挑戰者出現之前被轉化成真正的來源，才會變成護城河

opts.en: This proves the category has no possible moat
opts.zh: 這證明這個類別根本不可能有護城河

opts.en: This proves network effects don't exist in social platforms
opts.zh: 這證明社群平台不存在網路效應

exp.en: Being first buys a head start, not a moat — the pitfall named earlier in this lesson. If that lead never gets converted into a real switching cost or a genuine network effect, a later entrant with a better product and a faster growth loop can and does take the users away, exactly as happened here.
exp.zh: 先進場買到的是起步優勢，不是護城河——這正是本課前面點名的陷阱。如果這個領先從沒被轉化成真正的轉換成本或真正的網路效應，一個產品更好、成長飛輪更快的後進者，完全可以、也確實會把用戶搶走，就像這個案例發生的一樣。

q.en: You are testing a company for a moat by comparing its gross margin with its closest peer's. The only three years of data you have are the three years of a severe industry-wide shortage, when both companies posted record margins. What is the main problem with that comparison?
q.zh: 你想用「和最接近的同業比毛利率」來檢驗一家公司有沒有護城河，但手上只拿得到三年資料，而這三年剛好都是全產業嚴重缺貨、兩家公司毛利率都創新高的年份。這樣比較的主要問題是什麼？

opts.en: No problem — a boom is exactly when the stronger company pulls furthest ahead of the weaker one
opts.zh: 沒有問題——景氣大好的時候，正是強者把弱者甩得最開的時候

opts.en: A shortage lifts the weaker producer the most, so the peer gap is at its narrowest precisely then — the comparison will understate the difference between them
