q.en: A durable, high-quality compounder falls 55% from its peak over eighteen months, while its competitive position, margins, and growth drivers show no sign of deterioration. What does this framework say about that drawdown?
q.zh: 一檔體質很好、持久的複利股，在十八個月內從高點跌了 55%，而它的競爭地位、毛利率、成長動能都沒有惡化的跡象。這套框架對這次回撤怎麼看？

opts.en: A drawdown that deep always means the market has spotted a real, undisclosed problem with the business.
opts.zh: 這麼深的回撤，一定代表市場察覺到某個生意本身還沒揭露的真正問題。

opts.en: A drawdown of that magnitude is well within normal for a great business and, by itself, is not evidence the thesis has broken.
opts.zh: 這種幅度的回撤，對一門很棒的生意來說完全在正常範圍內，光憑這一點，並不是論點破功的證據。

opts.en: The position should be automatically doubled, since a big drawdown with no fundamental change is always a buying opportunity.
opts.zh: 應該自動加倍部位，因為基本面沒變的大幅回撤永遠是加碼機會。

exp.en: Both Amazon (1999-2001) and Netflix (2011) fell by roughly this magnitude or more while the underlying business went on to compound for years. A deep drawdown does not, by itself, tell you whether a thesis has broken — that judgment comes from the moat and durability tools, not the price move.
exp.zh: 亞馬遜（1999–2001）跟網飛（2011）都曾經跌到這個幅度甚至更深，而底層生意接下來都持續複利了好幾年。深度回撤本身，並不會告訴你論點是不是破功了——這個判斷來自護城河跟持久性工具，不是股價的變動本身。

q.en: Two retirement portfolios share the exact same average annual return over twenty years and both withdraw a fixed dollar amount every year. Portfolio A takes a 30% drawdown in year one; Portfolio B takes an identical 30% drawdown in year nineteen. What happens?
q.zh: 兩個退休組合在二十年間有完全相同的平均年化報酬率，兩者每年都提領固定金額。A 組合在第一年就遇到 30% 回撤；B 組合在第十九年才遇到一模一樣的 30% 回撤。結果會怎樣？

opts.en: Portfolio A ends with meaningfully less money, because the early drawdown forced years of withdrawals from an already-depleted share base.
opts.zh: A 組合最後金額明顯較少，因為早期的回撤，讓接下來好幾年的提領，都是從一個已經被削減的股數基礎裡進行。

opts.en: Both end with the same amount of money, since the average return is identical.
opts.zh: 兩者最後金額相同，因為平均報酬率一模一樣。

opts.en: Portfolio B ends with less money, because a later drawdown always does more damage.
opts.zh: B 組合最後金額較少，因為越晚發生的回撤傷害一定越大。

exp.en: This is sequence-of-returns risk: the same average return produces different ending outcomes depending on when a deep drawdown lands relative to fixed withdrawals. Early drawdowns combined with ongoing withdrawals permanently shrink the compounding base.
exp.zh: 這就是報酬順序風險：同樣的平均報酬率，會因為深度回撤相對於固定提領的時間點不同，產生不同的最終結果。早期回撤加上持續提領，會永久縮小可以複利的股數基礎。

q.en: A research team computes a combined portfolio's net asset value by adding two dollar-value NAV curves directly, day by day, even though the two legs are meant to be held at fixed target weights. What is wrong with this?
q.zh: 一個研究團隊把兩條淨值曲線的美元數字逐日直接相加，算出合成組合的淨值，即使這兩條腿本來設計成要維持固定的目標權重。這樣做錯在哪裡？

opts.en: Nothing — as long as both legs started at the same dollar amount, direct addition is always correct.
opts.zh: 沒有錯——只要兩腿一開始的美元金額相同，直接相加永遠是對的。

opts.en: Direct addition implicitly lets whichever leg is worth more dollars on a given day silently dominate the combined number, drifting away from the intended fixed weight.
opts.zh: 直接相加隱含地讓當天美元金額較高的那一腿悄悄主導合成數字，讓結果偏離原本設定的固定權重。

opts.en: Direct addition is fine for computing returns but never for computing drawdown.
opts.zh: 直接相加算報酬率沒問題，但算回撤就一定不行。

exp.en: Portfolio-level NAV must be built from weighted returns computed each period, not from adding raw dollar curves — even matching starting dollars says nothing about whether the legs still deserve equal weight after performance diverges.
exp.zh: 組合層級的淨值必須從每期算出的加權報酬率建構出來，不能靠加總原始美元曲線——即使起始美元金額相同，也完全沒說明績效分道揚鑣之後，兩腿是不是仍然值得相同的權重。

q.en: An analyst says: 'This portfolio has 22 tickers, so it is well diversified, and there is no need to check anything else.' What is the most likely error in this statement?
q.zh: 一位分析者說：「這個組合有 22 檔股票，所以已經算充分分散了，不需要再檢查別的。」這句話最可能犯的錯誤是什麼？

opts.en: 22 is too small a number for any portfolio to be diversified.
opts.zh: 22 檔對任何組合來說都是太小的數字，不可能算分散。

opts.en: 22 tickers is fine, but only if they are all in the same sector.
opts.zh: 22 檔是可以的，但前提是全部都要在同一個產業裡。

opts.en: Ticker count alone says nothing about whether several of those 22 positions share one underlying driver.
opts.zh: 單純的持股檔數，完全沒有回答那 22 檔裡有沒有好幾檔共用同一個底層驅動因子。

exp.en: A high ticker count with unchecked clustering is the exact ARKK-style mistake: many names can still be one concentrated bet wearing different costumes.
exp.zh: 沒檢查群聚的高持股檔數，正是 ARKK 那種錯誤：很多檔名字底下，仍然可能是同一個集中賭注穿著不同的戲服。

q.en: A portfolio's stock sleeve has 4 satellite positions each capped at 6% of total assets, alongside core positions. The satellite count is raised to 7 without changing the cap per position. What is the most direct consequence for the core positions?
q.zh: 一個個股部有 4 檔衛星部位，各自占總資產上限 6%，另外還有核心部位。衛星檔數提高到 7 檔，每檔上限不變。這對核心部位最直接的影響是什麼？

opts.en: The combined satellite budget grows, leaving a smaller residual stock-sleeve budget available for core positions, since both draw from the same sleeve.
opts.zh: 衛星合計預算變大，留給核心部位的剩餘個股部預算就變小，因為兩者共用同一塊個股部預算。

opts.en: None — satellite and core budgets are always calculated independently of each other.
opts.zh: 沒有影響——衛星跟核心的預算永遠是各自獨立計算的。

opts.en: Core position caps automatically rise to compensate.
opts.zh: 核心部位的上限會自動提高來補償。

exp.en: Satellites and core positions both draw from the same fixed stock-sleeve budget. Raising satellite count while holding the per-satellite cap fixed increases the combined satellite draw and shrinks what is left for core — exactly what the calculator in this lesson makes visible.
exp.zh: 衛星跟核心部位共用同一塊固定的個股部預算。在每檔衛星上限不變的情況下提高檔數，會讓衛星合計占用的預算變大，壓縮留給核心的空間——這正是這一課的試算器讓人看得到的東西。

q.en: An index position's weekly close sits above its 52-week moving average for eleven straight weeks, then dips one dollar below it for a single Tuesday before recovering by Friday. Under the weekly-close gate described in this lesson, what happens?
q.zh: 某個指數部位的週收盤價連續 11 週高於 52 週均線，之後有一個星期二盤中跌破均線一美元，週五又收回上方。依這一課講的週收盤閘門，會發生什麼事？

opts.en: The position is exited on Tuesday and re-entered on Friday
opts.zh: 部位在週二被出場，週五再重新進場

opts.en: The moving average itself resets to that day's intraday low
opts.zh: 均線本身會重設到那天的盤中低點

opts.en: Nothing — the gate only reads Friday's close, and Friday closed above the line
opts.zh: 什麼事都不會發生——閘門只讀週五收盤，而週五收盤仍在均線之上

opts.en: The gate becomes unreliable for the rest of the year after any intraday breach
opts.zh: 只要出現任何盤中跌破，閘門在該年度剩下的時間都會變得不可靠

exp.en: The gate is defined on the weekly closing price, so an intraday dip that fully recovers before the checkpoint never registers as a signal at all. The tempting wrong answer is the first one, which quietly assumes the rule is watching price continuously; a rule that reacted to that Tuesday would have paid a round trip in costs to end the week holding exactly what it started with.
exp.zh: 閘門是定義在週收盤價上的，所以一次在檢查點之前就完全收回的盤中下探，根本不會被登記成訊號。最誘人的錯誤答案是第一個，它悄悄假設了規則在連續盯著價格；一條真的對那個星期二做出反應的規則，會付掉一趟來回的交易成本，最後在週末持有的東西跟週初一模一樣。

q.en: σ_realized is 12.5% and σ_target is 15.0%, with a cap of 150%. What is the capped raw exposure ratio?
q.zh: σ_realized 為 12.5%，σ_target 為 15.0%，天花板為 150%。套過天花板之後的原始曝險比率是多少？

opts.en: About 120%
About 83%
About 150%
About 27.5%

exp.en: 15.0% ÷ 12.5% = 120%, which is below the 150% ceiling, so the cap does not bind and the ratio passes through unchanged. The 83% answer is the same division performed upside down — a genuinely common slip, and one that points the position the wrong way, cutting exposure in a market that is calmer than its own norm rather than adding to it.
exp.zh: 15.0% ÷ 12.5% ＝ 120%，低於 150% 的天花板，所以天花板沒有夾限，比率原封不動地通過。「約 83%」是把同一個除法上下顛倒的結果——這是很常見的失手，而且它會把部位推向完全相反的方向：在一個比自身常態更平靜的市場裡減碼，而不是加碼。

q.en: Why is the exposure cap set at 1.5× rather than, say, 3×, given that a higher cap would let the sizing formula respond more fully during unusually calm markets?
q.zh: 為什麼曝險天花板設在 1.5 倍，而不是例如 3 倍——畢竟更高的天花板能讓部位大小算式在異常平靜的市場中反應得更完整？

opts.en: A higher cap is mechanically impossible to calculate
opts.zh: 更高的天花板在數學上根本算不出來

opts.en: The cap has no effect on outcomes either way
opts.zh: 天花板設多高其實對結果毫無影響

opts.en: A higher cap would make the weekly gate check unnecessary
opts.zh: 天花板設更高，每週的閘門檢查就沒有必要了

opts.en: Losses and drag both scale badly with the multiple — a −30% month costs far more at 3× than at 1.5×, and volatility drag grows with the square of the multiple while the expected gain grows only linearly
opts.zh: 虧損與拖累都會隨倍數惡化——同樣的 −30% 月份在 3 倍下遠比 1.5 倍慘烈，而波動拖累隨倍數的平方成長，期望增益卻只隨倍數線性成長

exp.en: A −30% month costs 1.5 × (−30%) = −45% at the lower cap and 3 × (−30%) = −90% at the higher one, and on a 20%-volatility asset the annual drag runs roughly 1.5% at 1.5× against roughly 12% at 3×. Both penalties climb faster than the multiple while the expected benefit climbs only in step with it, which is why the sensible ceiling stops well short of what a margin account would technically allow.
exp.zh: 一個 −30% 的月份，在較低的天花板下是 1.5 × (−30%) ＝ −45%，在較高的天花板下是 3 × (−30%) ＝ −90%；而在一個波動率 20% 的資產上，1.5 倍的年化拖累大約 1.5%，3 倍大約 12%。兩種懲罰的成長速度都快過倍數本身，期望利益卻只跟著倍數等比上升——這正是為什麼合理的天花板，會遠低於融資帳戶技術上允許的水準。

q.en: Current holding is 60%, the raw capped ratio this week computes to 72%, and the threshold is 20 percentage points. What happens?
q.zh: 目前持倉為 60%，這一週算出的原始已夾限比率為 72%，門檻為 20 個百分點。會發生什麼事？

opts.en: A trade fires immediately to bring the position to exactly 72%
opts.zh: 立刻觸發交易，把部位調整到剛好 72%

opts.en: No trade — the 12-point gap is below the 20-point threshold, so the position is left alone
opts.zh: 不下單——12 個百分點的差距低於 20 個百分點的門檻，所以部位維持不動

opts.en: The gate closes because the target ratio moved
opts.zh: 因為目標比率有變化，閘門會關閉

opts.en: The cap is breached, forcing an emergency exit
opts.zh: 天花板被突破，觸發緊急出場

exp.en: 72% − 60% = 12 percentage points, below the 20-point threshold, so the band deliberately holds still. The first option is the instinct the band exists to override: the theoretical target does move every week, and acting on every move is what turns a low-frequency rule into a high-cost one.
exp.zh: 72% − 60% ＝ 12 個百分點，低於 20 個百分點的門檻，所以執行帶刻意按兵不動。第一個選項正是執行帶存在的目的所要壓下去的本能：理論目標每週都在動，而對每一次移動都出手，正是把一條低頻規則變成高成本規則的原因。

q.en: A portfolio holds two instruments under a shared 150% portfolio cap, so each leg carries an effective 75% share. Grid rounding pushes leg one from a raw 74% to 80%, and leg two from a raw 73% to 80%. Each leg on a raw basis still looked under its share. What is the actual problem?
q.zh: 一個組合在共用的 150% 組合天花板下持有兩個標的，所以每一條腿的有效份額是 75%。格點取整把第一條腿的原始值 74% 推到 80%，第二條腿的原始值 73% 也推到 80%。就原始數字看，每一條腿都還低於自己的份額。真正的問題是什麼？

opts.en: There is no problem — both legs are individually fine
opts.zh: 沒有問題——兩條腿個別看都沒事

opts.en: The gate should close for both legs simultaneously
opts.zh: 兩條腿的閘門應該同時關閉

opts.en: The rounded sum is 160%, above the 150% portfolio cap, so the clamp has to be applied to the summed total rather than checked leg by leg
opts.zh: 取整後加總是 160%，超過 150% 的組合天花板，所以夾限必須套用在加總後的總額上，而不是逐條腿分別檢查

opts.en: Grid rounding should be abandoned entirely for multi-leg portfolios
opts.zh: 多腿組合應該完全放棄格點取整

exp.en: 80% + 80% = 160%, ten points over the portfolio ceiling, even though every individual piece looked compliant — two independent roundings happened to push the same way at the same time. The last option overcorrects: rounding is what keeps the trade list coarse and cheap; the fix is ordering, round each leg, sum, then clamp the total.
exp.zh: 80% ＋ 80% ＝ 160%，比組合天花板多出十個百分點，即使每一小塊個別看起來都合規——兩次獨立的取整剛好在同一時間往同一個方向推。最後一個選項則是矯枉過正：取整正是讓交易清單維持粗糙、便宜的機制；解法是順序問題——先各腿取整、加總，再對總額夾限。

q.en: A backtest compares a 10-point execution-band threshold against a 20-point threshold and finds the wider band trades about half as often and earns a slightly higher return over the sample tested. What is the most defensible conclusion?
q.zh: 一次回測比較 10 個百分點與 20 個百分點的執行帶門檻，發現較寬的門檻換手頻率大約減半，而且在測試樣本裡報酬率略高一些。最站得住腳的結論是什麼？

opts.en: Wider bands always produce higher returns because they cut friction
opts.zh: 門檻越寬，報酬率一定越高，因為降低了摩擦成本

opts.en: The result shows the threshold should be widened further without limit
opts.zh: 這個結果顯示門檻應該無限繼續拓寬下去

opts.en: Trading frequency has no reliable relationship to the threshold chosen
opts.zh: 換手頻率跟門檻設定之間沒有可靠的關係

opts.en: The frequency reduction is close to mechanical, but the return improvement is sample-specific and needs checking across other windows and regimes before being trusted
opts.zh: 換手減少幾乎是機械式的必然，但報酬改善是樣本特定的結果，需要跨其他時間窗口與市場環境檢驗過才能相信

exp.en: Fewer trades from a wider band is close to guaranteed; whether the saved friction outweighs sitting further from the ideal exposure is a separate, sample-dependent question. In one documented audit, rotating a detail nobody had treated as a parameter — which weekday the weekly close is sampled on — reversed the same apparent improvement on four of five choices.
exp.zh: 門檻拓寬帶來換手減少，幾乎是必然的；但省下的摩擦成本，是否蓋得過「停留在離理想曝險更遠處」的代價，是另一個依賴樣本的問題。在一次有紀錄的審計裡，把一個沒人當成參數看待的細節——週線收盤取星期幾——輪流換過之後，同樣那個看似的改善在五種選擇中的四種都反轉成了下降。

q.en: A system computes exposure as a decimal fraction and fires a trade only when abs(raw − current) >= 0.20. A position sits at 0.80 and the raw target computes to 1.00. What is the risk in this implementation, even though the gap looks like precisely 0.20?
q.zh: 一套系統用小數分數計算曝險，並且只在 abs(原始值 − 目前值) >= 0.20 成立時才觸發交易。某個部位停在 0.80，原始目標算出來是 1.00。即使差距看起來剛好是 0.20，這個實作有什麼風險？

opts.en: Floating-point subtraction can land on 0.19999999 instead of exactly 0.2, silently skipping the trade the rule intended to fire
opts.zh: 浮點數減法可能得到 0.19999999 而不是精確的 0.2，悄悄漏掉這條規則原本要觸發的交易

opts.en: None — 1.00 minus 0.80 is always exactly 0.20 in any implementation
opts.zh: 沒有風險——1.00 減 0.80 在任何實作裡都一定剛好等於 0.20

opts.en: The gate closes automatically whenever this happens
opts.zh: 每次發生這種情況，閘門會自動關閉

opts.en: It only matters when the cap is set above 150%
opts.zh: 這只有在天花板設在 150% 以上時才有影響

exp.en: Binary floating point cannot store every decimal fraction exactly, so a comparison written in decimal space can miss a value that is mathematically sitting on the threshold — and those exact-on-the-line cases are common, because a previous trade just rounded the position to a clean grid value. Converting to whole percentage-point integers before comparing removes the ambiguity.
exp.zh: 二進位浮點數無法精確儲存每一個小數分數，所以用小數空間寫的比較式，可能漏掉一個數學上恰好落在門檻上的數值——而這種「剛好壓線」的情況並不罕見，因為前一次交易才剛把部位取整到一個乾淨的格點值。把比較先換算成整數百分點，就能消除這個模糊地帶。

q.en: A results table shows the same gate-and-volatility-target mechanism producing a Calmar ratio of about 0.60 on a US index pair tested from 2005, and about 1.22 on a Taiwan index pair tested from 2014. What is the most defensible reading?
q.zh: 一張結果表顯示，同一套閘門加波動率目標的機制，在一組自 2005 年起測試的美股指數標的上 Calmar 約 0.60，在一組自 2014 年起測試的台股指數標的上約 1.22。最站得住腳的讀法是什麼？

opts.en: The mechanism is roughly twice as effective in Taiwan as in the United States
opts.zh: 這套機制在台灣的有效程度大約是在美國的兩倍

opts.en: The two rows cover different decades — the 2014 start skips the 2008 crisis the other row had to survive — so the ratios describe two market histories, not two qualities of the mechanism
opts.zh: 兩列涵蓋的是不同的十年——2014 年起算跳過了另一列必須熬過的 2008 年危機——所以這兩個比率描述的是兩段市場歷史，不是這套機制的兩種品質

opts.en: Calmar is stable enough that a decade of data settles the comparison
opts.zh: Calmar 夠穩定，十年的資料足以為這個比較定案

opts.en: The gap proves the volatility target contributed more in one market than in the other
opts.zh: 這個差距證明波動率目標在其中一個市場的貢獻大於另一個

exp.en: Calmar divides a return by one realized worst case, so a sample that never contained a 2008 is not comparable to one that did, and a single deeper drawdown in the next decade would move either number substantially. The last option fails for a different reason: both rows ran the gate and the sizing layer switched on together, so nothing in the table can separate the two contributions.
exp.zh: Calmar 是用報酬去除以一次已實現的最差情況，所以一個從未包含 2008 年的樣本，跟一個包含了的樣本不能直接比；未來十年只要出現一次更深的回撤，任一個數字都會大幅移動。最後一個選項錯在另一個理由：兩列都是閘門與部位大小層一起開著跑的，所以表格裡沒有任何東西能把兩者的貢獻拆開。

q.en: Two researchers test the same trend-following rule across lookback windows from 20 to 80 weeks. Researcher A gets the best result at exactly 47 weeks, with performance falling off sharply at 45 and at 49. Researcher B gets a slightly lower but nearly identical result anywhere between 40 and 60 weeks. Whose rule is more likely to keep working, and why?
q.zh: 兩位研究者用 20 週到 80 週的回顧期，測試同一條趨勢跟蹤規則。研究者甲在剛好 47 週拿到最好的結果，45 週與 49 週的表現則明顯掉下來。研究者乙在 40 週到 60 週之間，都拿到略低但幾乎相同的結果。哪一位的規則比較可能繼續有用，為什麼？

opts.en: Researcher A's, because a higher score measured on the same history is direct evidence of a stronger edge
opts.zh: 研究者甲的，因為在同一段歷史上量出更高的分數，就是優勢更強的直接證據

opts.en: Researcher B's, because a wide flat plateau suggests the edge lives in the mechanism, while a narrow spike is a fingerprint of this particular stretch of history
opts.zh: 研究者乙的，因為一片寬闊平坦的高原代表優勢住在機制裡，而一個狹窄的尖峰只是這一段特定歷史的指紋

opts.en: Neither can be judged without first knowing both Sharpe ratios
opts.zh: 在還沒知道兩邊的夏普比率之前，兩個都無法判斷

opts.en: Researcher A's, because a sharp peak shows the rule has been precisely calibrated to the market
opts.zh: 研究者甲的，因為一個銳利的尖峰代表這條規則已經被精準校準到市場上

exp.en: The response surface, not the peak score, is what a parameter sweep is actually good for. A rule that works across 40 to 60 weeks is saying the specific number barely matters, which is what a real mechanism looks like; a rule that works only at 47 is describing this sample. The counter-intuitive part is that the correct move is to deliberately give up the highest score and take the plateau instead — the peak is where the fit is, the plateau is where the mechanism is.
exp.zh: 參數掃描真正的用處是看響應曲面，不是看最高分。一條在 40 週到 60 週之間都成立的規則，等於在說具體用幾週幾乎不重要，這正是真實機制該有的樣子；一條只在 47 週成立的規則，描述的是這一份樣本。反直覺的地方在於，正確的做法是刻意放棄最高分、改選高原——山頂是擬合待的地方，高原才是機制待的地方。

q.en: A backtest of an earnings-quality rule uses a financial database that stores only the current, restated version of each company's historical figures. What problem does this most likely create?
q.zh: 一份盈餘品質規則的回測，用的財務資料庫只存了每家公司歷史數字「現在、已重編過」的版本。這最可能製造什麼問題？

opts.en: Survivorship bias, because companies that later failed are excluded from the database entirely
opts.zh: 存活者偏誤，因為後來失敗的公司整個被排除在資料庫之外

opts.en: Timing luck, because the rebalancing date was never treated as a free parameter
opts.zh: 時機運氣，因為再平衡日期從來沒有被當成自由參數處理

opts.en: No problem, since the restated figures are more accurate now than the originally reported ones
opts.zh: 沒有問題，因為重編後的數字比當初公布的數字更準確

opts.en: Look-ahead bias, because the rule may be scored on corrected information no investor holding the stock at that date could have had
opts.zh: 前視偏誤，因為規則可能是用修正後的資訊打的分數，而那個時點持有這檔股票的投資人根本拿不到那份資訊

exp.en: Restated figures really are more accurate today, which is exactly what makes the third option tempting — but accuracy is not the test. The test is availability at the historical date being traded, and a cleaned-up database quietly hands the rule information nobody had at the time. Survivorship bias is a different failure: it is about which companies appear at all, not about which version of their numbers is used.
exp.zh: 重編後的數字現在確實更準確，這正是第三個選項誘人的原因——但這裡要檢驗的不是準確度，而是「在那個被交易的歷史時點取不取得到」。一個已經清理乾淨的資料庫，等於悄悄把當時沒人拿得到的資訊塞給規則。存活者偏誤是另一種失效：它談的是哪些公司有沒有被納入，不是用了哪一個版本的數字。

q.en: A research team tests 150 variations of a trading rule against the same twenty years of market data and publishes the single best-performing variation, with a Sharpe ratio of 2.4. Roughly what does the multiple-comparisons calculator in this lesson suggest about that number?
q.zh: 一個研究團隊用同一段二十年的市場資料，測試了 150 種交易規則的變體，只發表其中表現最好的那個版本，夏普比率 2.4。這一課的多重比較試算器大致上會提示你什麼？

opts.en: A Sharpe ratio of 2.4 is high enough that luck can be ruled out regardless of how many variations were tested
opts.zh: 夏普比率 2.4 已經高到不管測了多少個變體，都可以排除運氣的可能

opts.en: The number of variations tested is irrelevant as long as the single best one is the one published
opts.zh: 只要發表的是表現最好的那一個，測過幾個變體根本不重要

opts.en: With 150 variations tested, finding at least one that looks significant purely by chance is close to certain, so the 2.4 figure needs independent out-of-sample confirmation before it means anything
opts.zh: 測了 150 個變體，純靠運氣就找到至少一個看起來顯著的結果，機率幾乎是必然，所以這個 2.4 在有獨立樣本外驗證之前，還不能說明什麼

opts.en: 150 variations is far too few to create any meaningful multiple-comparisons risk
opts.zh: 150 個變體太少了，遠不足以構成有意義的多重比較風險

exp.en: At even a modest 5% per-test luck rate, 150 tested variations pushes the probability that at least one looks significant purely by chance to well above 99%. What should set the reader's skepticism is the number of variations tried, not the size of the Sharpe ratio on its own — which is why the most useful single question to ask about any backtest is how many versions were tried before this one.
exp.zh: 即使每次測試只有 5% 的運氣率，測了 150 個變體，也會讓「至少一個純靠運氣看起來顯著」的機率被推到遠超過 99%。決定讀者該有多懷疑的，是試過的變體數量，不是單看夏普比率本身——這也是為什麼對任何一份回測，最有用的一個問題就是「在這個版本之前，一共試過幾個版本」。

q.en: A systematic research team widens an execution-layer threshold specifically to reduce how often the system trades. As a side effect, one market's reported Calmar ratio also improves. What is the correct first response?
q.zh: 一個規則化研究團隊放寬了執行層門檻，動機明確是要降低系統交易的頻率。結果作為副作用，某個市場的卡瑪比率也跟著變好了。正確的第一反應應該是什麼？

opts.en: Publish the improved Calmar ratio immediately as evidence the change also boosted returns
opts.zh: 立刻把變好的卡瑪比率公布出來，當成這個改動也提升報酬的證據

opts.en: Reverse the threshold change, since any unexplained improvement is automatically suspicious
opts.zh: 直接撤回這個門檻改動，因為任何說不清楚原因的改善都自動可疑

opts.en: Ignore the Calmar change entirely, since the original goal was trade frequency rather than returns
opts.zh: 完全忽略卡瑪比率的變化，因為原本的目標是交易頻率，不是報酬

opts.en: Treat the improvement as timing luck until a dedicated audit — rerunning the identical rule across every reasonable implementation-detail choice — says otherwise
opts.zh: 在專門的審計——把完全相同的規則套用在每一個合理的實作細節選項上重跑一遍——證明不是之前，先把這個改善當成時機運氣

exp.en: This is the timing-luck war story exactly: an execution-layer change made for one stated reason produced a side-effect improvement in a risk-adjusted return metric, and the audit across five weekday anchors found the improvement held on only one of the five — the one already in production. Ignoring the change entirely is the closest wrong answer, because the number still has to be prevented from being cited later as a reason to loosen the same threshold again.
exp.zh: 這正是時機運氣那則戰爭故事的型態：一個為了某個明講理由而做的執行層改動，順帶讓一項風險調整報酬指標變好，而跨五個週幾錨點的審計發現，這個改善只在五個選項裡的一個成立——正是已經在實際使用的那一個。最接近的錯誤答案是「完全忽略」，因為這個數字還是得被擋下來，不能日後被拿去當作「所以再放寬同一個門檻」的理由。

q.en: A performance comparison table shows “Configuration A, 1.5× leverage” next to “Configuration B, 1.0× leverage,” with every number in both columns calculated correctly. What additional check does this lesson recommend before trusting it as a clean leverage comparison?
q.zh: 一張績效對照表把「配置 A，1.5 倍槓桿」跟「配置 B，1.0 倍槓桿」並排放在一起，兩欄裡的每個數字都算對了。這一課建議在把它當成乾淨的槓桿對照之前，還要多做什麼檢查？

opts.en: Confirm from the footnotes that the execution rules, time window, and every other setting besides leverage are genuinely identical between the two columns
opts.zh: 從註腳確認執行規則、時間窗口，以及除了槓桿以外的其他每一項設定，在兩欄之間是不是真的完全一致

opts.en: Recalculate every number in both columns to check for arithmetic errors
opts.zh: 重新算一次兩欄裡的每個數字，檢查有沒有算術錯誤

opts.en: Assume the table is accurate, since both columns came out of the same research process
opts.zh: 假設表格是準確的，因為兩欄都來自同一個研究流程

opts.en: Discard the table, since any leverage comparison is inherently unreliable
opts.zh: 直接捨棄這張表，因為任何槓桿對照本質上都不可靠

exp.en: This is the apples-to-apples war story: every individual number was arithmetically correct, so recalculating finds nothing. The two columns silently differed in a second variable — the execution ruleset — besides the one the table claimed to be about, and only reading the footnotes for what else changed catches it.
exp.zh: 這正是同條件比較那則戰爭故事：每一個數字本身的算術都是對的，所以重算什麼都查不到。兩欄之間悄悄地不只差了表格宣稱要比較的那一個變數，還差了第二個變數——執行規則集，只有去讀註腳確認還有什麼變了，才抓得到這件事。

q.en: A published long-run backtest reports strong performance for the full 2005–2024 sample. A closer look shows almost all of its edge over a passive benchmark came from 2009–2021, with no advantage — and briefly a disadvantage — during the 2008–2009 and 2020 crash windows. What is this a failure to do?
q.zh: 一份公開的長期回測公布了 2005 到 2024 年整段樣本的強勁表現。仔細一看，它相對於被動基準的優勢，幾乎全部來自 2009 到 2021 年，在 2008 到 2009 年與 2020 年這兩段崩盤窗口裡沒有優勢，甚至一度更差。這是沒有做到什麼？

opts.en: Adjust prices for stock splits and dividends
opts.zh: 對股價做拆股與配息的還原調整

opts.en: Model trading costs explicitly
opts.zh: 把交易成本顯性建模進去

opts.en: Report performance broken down by sub-period or market regime, instead of only a full-sample average that buries where the edge actually came from
opts.zh: 依子期間或市場狀態拆分報告表現，而不是只給一個藏起優勢真正來源的全樣本平均數

opts.en: Use a point-in-time universe
opts.zh: 使用時點正確的母體

exp.en: This is the regime-reporting rule from the worked example's sixth question. A single full-sample number can conceal that a strategy's entire edge came from one favorable stretch and vanished, or reversed, exactly when an investor would most have wanted protection — and unlike the other three options, nothing about the data construction here is wrong, only what got reported.
exp.zh: 這正是逐步範例第六個問題所示範的分期報告規則。一個單一的全樣本數字，可以把「一套策略全部的優勢都來自某一段有利行情、而且在投資人最需要保護的時候消失甚至反轉」這件事完全藏起來——而且跟另外三個選項不同，這裡的資料建構本身並沒有錯，錯的只是報告方式。

q.en: What is the one thing this lesson argues no backtest can ever validate, no matter how carefully it corrects for survivorship bias, look-ahead bias, timing luck, and every other issue this lesson covers?
q.zh: 這一課主張，不管一份回測把存活者偏誤、前視偏誤、時機運氣，以及這一課提到的每一個問題都修正得多仔細，有一件事它永遠無法驗證。是什麼？

opts.en: The exact starting price of the instrument being tested
opts.zh: 被測試標的確切的起始價格

opts.en: Whether the trading rule can be coded correctly
opts.zh: 這條交易規則能不能被正確寫成程式

opts.en: The tax treatment of any gains the rule produces
opts.zh: 這條規則產生的獲利該怎麼課稅

opts.en: A market regime, or a kind of day, that never occurred anywhere inside the sample the backtest was built on
opts.zh: 一種從沒在回測建構所用的樣本裡出現過的市場狀態，或那樣的一天

exp.en: This is the explicit boundary this lesson states: a backtest can only describe the range of conditions its sample actually lived through. No amount of methodological rigor manufactures evidence about a kind of day the market has not yet had — which is exactly the gap that destroyed the note in this lesson's opening case, and the reason the correct response is to size with room to survive it rather than to distrust every number.
exp.zh: 這正是這一課明講的邊界：一份回測只能描述它的樣本實際經歷過的條件範圍。不管方法論做得多嚴謹，都沒辦法對一種市場還沒經歷過的日子憑空生出證據——這正是這一課開場案例裡把那檔票券毀掉的那個落差，也是為什麼正確的回應是「把部位留出能撐過那一天的空間」，而不是「不信任每一個數字」。

q.en: A research process only ever publishes the rules that cleared its adoption bar, quietly discarding every configuration that was tested and failed. What principle from this lesson does this violate?
q.zh: 一個研究流程只發表通過採用門檻的規則，悄悄丟掉每一個測試過但沒通過的版本。這違反了這一課的哪個原則？

opts.en: Negative or null results deserve the same rigor and visibility as positive ones — silently discarding failed tests recreates the multiple-comparisons problem at the institutional level
opts.zh: 負面或無效的結果應該得到跟正面結果同等的嚴謹度與能見度——悄悄丟掉沒通過的測試，等於在制度層級重新製造了多重比較的問題

opts.en: Backtests must always use adjusted prices
opts.zh: 回測一律要用還原股價

opts.en: Every rule needs a walk-forward test
opts.zh: 每一條規則都需要前進式驗證

opts.en: Trading costs must be modeled explicitly
opts.zh: 交易成本必須顯性建模

exp.en: Only showing what worked while hiding every configuration that failed a pre-registered test is exactly the multiple-comparisons illusion from this lesson's calculator, applied at the level of an entire research pipeline rather than a single parameter sweep. The other three options are all real rules from this lesson, but none of them is about what happens to the results nobody publishes.
exp.zh: 只展示成功的結果、卻藏起每一個沒通過預先設定測試的版本，正是這一課試算器示範的多重比較幻覺，只是套用在整條研究流程的層級，而不是單一參數掃描的層級。另外三個選項都是這一課裡真實存在的規則，但沒有一條談的是「沒被發表出來的那些結果後來怎麼了」。
